overall.assessment: Prema prikazanoj strukturi, podcast je uglavnom usmjeren na Krista: molitva Božjem milosrđu i marijanska pobožnost vode prema pouzdanju, a tumačenje Pavlove radosti i poniznosti potiče slušatelja da se raduje širenju Evanđelja i kad ga naviješta netko drugi. Naglasci na nenametljivom prihvaćanju služenja, strpljivom čekanju i svjedočenju iz osobnog iskustva mogu podržati dostojanstvo osobe i kulturu susreta, ako se svjedočanstvo ne pretvori u mjerilo tuđe vjere. Ipak, sažetak ostavlja otvorenim kako su objašnjeni izrazi o vezivanju zlih sila, prvenstvu srca nad razumom i rezultatima kao štitu: potrebno ih je tumačiti kao molitvu pod Božjom vlašću, osjećaj prožet razborom te plodove koji se ne poistovjećuju s mjerom Božjeg blagoslova. Društvena dimenzija Evanđelja naznačena je zajedništvom i pozivom na podršku centru, ali iz strukture se ne vidi snažniji razvoj solidarnosti, općeg dobra ni povlaštene brige za siromašne.
seeds_of_logos: Molitva Božjem milosrđu, predanje Presvetom Srcu Isusovu i pouzdanje u teškim trenucima usmjeravaju prema Bogu kao izvoru milosrđa i nade.
Radosna otajstva i marijanska pobožnost mogu usmjeriti pogled prema Kristovu utjelovljenju i Mariji kao učenici koja prati Božje djelovanje.
Pavlova radost zbog navještaja koji šire drugi potiče slobodu od zavisti i natjecanja te zajedništvo u poslanju Crkve.
Poniznost i spremnost na posljednje mjesto odražavaju evanđeosko odbacivanje samouzvisivanja i poziv da se druge ne gleda s visoka.
Osobno svjedočanstvo i poziv na strpljivo čekanje s Gospodinom mogu ohrabriti nadu, ustrajnost i vjernost u služenju.
Poziv na podršku centru može postati konkretan čin solidarnosti i služenja, ako je povezan s transparentnošću, odgovornošću i stvarnim potrebama ljudi.
concerns: Izraz o vezivanju zlih sila treba jasno zadržati unutar kršćanskog razumijevanja molitve: kao zaziv Božje zaštite, a ne kao samostalnu tehniku ili formulu koja bi automatski jamčila duhovne ili zemaljske ishode.

Naglasak na srcu ne bi smio sugerirati da su razum, razboritost, provjera činjenica ili crkveno razlučivanje manje važni; kršćansko svjedočenje uključuje osjećaje, ali ih usklađuje s istinom i odgovornim prosuđivanjem.
Povezivanje vidljivih rezultata s potvrdom poslanja može skliznuti u uspjeh kao mjerilo Božjeg blagoslova; vjernost Evanđelju ne može se svesti na rast, priznanje ili uspjeh djelovanja.
Prema dostupnom sažetku nije moguće procijeniti jesu li osobno vodstvo, najave skupova i prikupljanje podrške prikazani transparentno, u crkvenom zajedništvu i bez pritiska na slušatelje.
overall.theological_context: Evangelii gaudium prikazuje evangelizaciju kao blizinu ljudima, slušanje njihovih briga i služenje njihovim duhovnim i materijalnim potrebama; isti dokument povezuje poniznost i nenametljivo svjedočenje s biblijskim pozivom da druge smatramo većima od sebe. Crkveno učenje o pučkoj pobožnosti vrednuje molitvene oblike poput krunice kada vode Kristu i žive se u zajedništvu Crkve, a ne kao puka vanjska praksa. Socijalni nauk Crkve traži da navještaj bude povezan sa solidarnošću, općim dobrom, sudjelovanjem i brigom za siromašne; milosrđe pritom ne isključuje istinu ni pravednost.

overall.assessment_en: According to the presented structure, the podcast is mainly focused on Christ: prayer to the Divine Mercy and Marian devotion lead toward trust, and the interpretation of Pauline joy and humility encourages the listener to rejoice in the spread of the Gospel even when it is proclaimed by someone else. The emphases on the unobtrusive acceptance of service, patient waiting, and witnessing from personal experience can support the dignity of the human person and the culture of encounter, provided that the testimony is not turned into a standard for another's faith. Nevertheless, the summary leaves open how expressions concerning the binding of evil forces, the primacy of the heart over reason, and results as a shield are explained: it is necessary to interpret them as prayer under God's authority, emotion permeated by prudence, and fruits that are not equated with the measure of God's blessing. The social dimension of the Gospel is indicated by fellowship and the call to support the center, but the structure does not show a stronger development of solidarity, the common good, or preferential care for the poor.
overall.theological_context_en: Evangelii gaudium depicts evangelization as closeness to people, listening to their concerns, and serving their spiritual and material needs; the same document connects humility and unobtrusive witnessing with the biblical call to regard others as greater than ourselves. Church teaching on popular piety values prayer forms like the Rosary when they lead to Christ and are lived in the communion of the Church, rather than as a mere external practice. The social doctrine of the Church requires that proclamation be connected with solidarity, the common good, participation, and care for the poor; in this, mercy does not exclude truth or justice.
seeds_of_logos_en: Prayer to the Divine Mercy, surrender to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, and trust in difficult moments direct toward God as the source of mercy and hope.
The joyful mysteries and Marian devotion can direct the gaze toward Christ's Incarnation and Mary as a disciple who accompanies God's action.
Paul's joy over the proclamation spread by others encourages freedom from envy and competition, as well as communion in the mission of the Church.
Humility and readiness for the last place reflect the Gospel rejection of self-exaltation and the call not to look down on others.
Personal testimony and the call to patient waiting with the Lord can encourage hope, perseverance, and fidelity in service.
The call to support the center can become a concrete act of solidarity and service, if it is linked with transparency, accountability, and the real needs of people.
concerns_en: The expression concerning the binding of evil forces should be clearly kept within a Christian understanding of prayer: as an invocation of God's protection, rather than as an independent technique or formula that would automatically guarantee spiritual or earthly outcomes.

The emphasis on the heart should not suggest that reason, prudence, fact-checking, or ecclesial discernment are less important; Christian witness includes emotions, but harmonizes them with truth and responsible judgment.

Connecting visible results with the confirmation of a mission can slide into success as a measure of God's blessing; fidelity to the Gospel cannot be reduced to growth, recognition, or the success of an activity.

According to the available summary, it is not possible to assess whether personal leadership, announcements of gatherings, and the gathering of support are presented transparently, in ecclesial communion, and without pressure on listeners.

sections.subtitle: Evanđelje koje postavlja ton: tko se ponizuje, bit će uzvišen
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar pozdravlja gledatelje i slušatelje medija Ora et Labora i čita evanđelje dana
sections.content:
Emisija počinje kratkim i jasnim pozdravom. Voditelj **Vladimir Grebenar** obraća se „dragim gledateljima i slušateljima medija Ora et Labora“ uobičajenim pozdravom „Pozdrav u Gospodinu“. Odmah zatim izgovara misao vodilju cijelog dana, evanđeoski redak koji će prožimati i kasnije tumačenje:

> „Koji se uzvisuje, bit će ponižen; a koji se ponizuje, bit će uzvišen.“

Nakon ove uvodne rečenice slijedi dugi i strukturirani molitveni blok. Grebenar ga ne prekida komentarima, nego vodi slušatelje kroz niz molitava. Redom se izmjenjuju molitve zaštite i posvete, Krunica i Litanije Božjem milosrđu te Gospina krunica s radosnim otajstvima. Evanđelje o poniznosti tako postaje okvir u koji se smješta sve što slijedi. Molitveni dio počinje znakom križa: „U ime Oca i Sina i Duha Svetoga. Amen.“

magisterium.assessment: Uvodni redak vjerno prenosi Isusovo učenje da će se oholi poniziti, a ponizni biti uzvišeni, što je izričito potvrđeno u Lk 14,11. Stavljanje molitve u okvir poniznosti dobro je usklađeno s kršćanskim naglaskom na Kristu kao uzoru poniznosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusova pouka nije samo poziv na društvenu skromnost nego na stav pred Bogom: odbacivanje samouzvisivanja i oslanjanje na Božju milost. Sveti Grgur Veliki povezuje Kristovu poniznost s našim pozivom na poniznost, a tumačenje pape Ivana Pavla II. ističe da se konačno uzvišenje poniznoga ostvaruje u Bogu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The opening line faithfully conveys Jesus' teaching that the proud will be humbled and the humble will be exalted, which is explicitly confirmed in Lk 14:11. Placing prayer within the framework of humility is well aligned with the Christian emphasis on Christ as the model of humility.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' instruction is not merely a call to social modesty but to an attitude before God: the rejection of self-exaltation and reliance on God's grace. Saint Gregory the Great connects Christ's humility with our call to humility, and Pope John Paul II's interpretation highlights that the ultimate exaltation of the humble person is realized in God.

sections.subtitle_en: The Gospel that sets the tone: whoever humbles himself will be exalted
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar greets the viewers and listeners of the Ora et Labora media and reads the gospel of the day
sections.content_en:
The show begins with a short and clear greeting. Host **Vladimir Grebenar** addresses the "dear viewers and listeners of the Ora et Labora media" with the customary greeting "Greetings in the Lord." Immediately thereafter, he speaks the guiding thought of the entire day, a gospel verse that will also permeate the later interpretation:

> "Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted."

After this introductory sentence follows a long and structured prayer block. Grebenar does not interrupt it with comments, but rather leads the listeners through a series of prayers. Prayers of protection and consecration, the Chaplet and Litany of the Divine Mercy, and the Rosary of Our Lady with the joyful mysteries alternate in turn. The Gospel of humility thus becomes the framework into which everything that follows is placed. The prayer part begins with the sign of the cross: "In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Amen."

sections.subtitle: Molitva oslobođenja: vezivanje zlih sila i plašt Marijine ljubavi nad obiteljima
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj moli molitvu oslobođenja i zaštite obitelji od zlih sila
sections.content:
Prva molitva ima izrazito zaštitni karakter. Vladimir Grebenar u ime Isusovo „uzima vlast“ i vezuje sve zle sile i snage. Molitva ih nabraja po mjestima na kojima djeluju:

- u zraku,
- na zemlji,
- u vodi,
- u podzemlju,
- na onome svijetu,
- u prirodi i u vatri.

Molitva zatim prelazi u slavljenje. Bog se ispovijeda kao **Gospodin nad svim svemirom**, a slava mu se daje u ime njegova stvorenja. Molitelji u Isusovo ime vezuju demonske sile „koje su došle protiv nas i naših obitelji“. Sve se stavlja pod zaštitu **dragocjene Kristove krvi**, prolivene na križu.

Važno mjesto ima i Marijin zagovor. Molitva traži zaštitu i posredovanje „kod Presvetog Srca Isusova za sve naše obitelji“, uz snažnu sliku: „Zaogrni nas ovim plaštem ljubavi, da se prestraši neprijatelj.“ U pomoć se zatim zazivaju **sveti Mihovil i anđeli čuvari**, da brane molitelje i njihove obitelji „u borbi protiv svega zla što obilazi svijetom“.

Vrhunac molitve je zapovijed svim silama zla da „odstupe istog časa“ od molitelja, njihovih domova i njihove zemlje. Molitva završava zahvalom Isusu, „jer si vjeran Bog i osjećaš s nama“.

magisterium.assessment: Zaštita obitelji molitvom, pouzdanje u Kristovu krv te zazivanje Marijina i anđeoskog zagovora mogu se uklopiti u katoličku pobožnost, a slični se zazivi nalaze i u crkvenim molitvama. Ipak, formulacija da molitelj „uzima vlast” nad zlim silama i zapovijeda im da odstupi može zamagliti razliku između ponizne molitve Bogu za zaštitu i izravnog, autoritativnog postupanja prema demonima.
concerns: Sažetak ne pokazuje izričito da se molba za zaštitu upućuje Bogu, nego opisuje osobno „uzimanje vlasti” i zapovijed zlim silama; takav jezik može stvoriti dojam da molitelj samostalno raspolaže duhovnom vlašću.
Navođenje zlih sila na mnogim područjima i traženje da odmah odstupi može, ako se shvati kao zajamčena formula, poticati magijsko razumijevanje molitve umjesto pouzdanja u Boga.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkvene molitve za zaštitu zazivaju Božju pomoć i zagovor Marije i svetoga Mihaela; službeni tekst, primjerice, moli Boga da odbije đavolsku moć i razriješi njezine okove, dok molitva svetomu Mihaelu traži njegovu obranu u borbi. Zato je teološki sigurnije shvatiti takve zazive kao prošnju Bogu za zaštitu, a ne kao tehniku ili jamstvo da se zlo mora povući na zapovijed pojedinog molitelja.

magisterium.assessment_en: Protecting the family through prayer, trusting in Christ's blood, and invoking Mary's and angelic intercession can fit into Catholic devotion, and similar invocations are found in Church prayers. Nevertheless, the formulation that the person praying „takes authority” over evil forces and commands them to depart can blur the distinction between humble prayer to God for protection and direct, authoritative action toward demons.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church's prayers for protection invoke God's help and the intercession of Mary and Saint Michael; an official text, for example, prays to God to repel diabolical power and loose its bonds, while the prayer to Saint Michael asks for his defense in battle. Therefore, it is theologically safer to understand such invocations as a petition to God for protection, rather than as a technique or guarantee that evil must retreat at the command of an individual person praying.
concerns_en: The summary does not show explicitly that the request for protection is addressed to God, but describes personally „taking authority” and commanding evil forces; such language can create the impression that the person praying independently disposes of spiritual authority.
Listing evil forces in many areas and demanding that they immediately depart can, if understood as a guaranteed formula, encourage a magical understanding of prayer instead of trust in God.

sections.subtitle_en: Prayer of deliverance: binding evil forces and the mantle of Mary's love over families
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host prays a prayer of deliverance and protection of families from evil forces
sections.content_en:
The first prayer has a distinctly protective character. Vladimir Grebenar in Jesus' name "takes authority" and binds all evil forces and powers. The prayer lists them according to the places in which they act:

- in the air,
- on the earth,
- in the water,
- in the underworld,
- in the other world,
- in nature and in fire.

The prayer then turns into praise. God is confessed as **Lord over all the universe**, and glory is given to him in the name of his creation. In Jesus' name, the pray-ers bind demonic forces "that have come against us and our families." Everything is placed under the protection of the **precious blood of Christ**, shed on the cross.

Mary's intercession also holds an important place. The prayer asks for protection and intercession "at the Sacred Heart of Jesus for all our families," with a powerful image: "Cover us with this mantle of love, so that the enemy may be terrified." **Saint Michael and the guardian angels** are then invoked for help, to defend the pray-ers and their families "in the fight against all evil that roams the world."

The climax of the prayer is a command to all powers of evil to "depart this very hour" from the pray-ers, their homes, and their land. The prayer ends with thanksgiving to Jesus, "because you are a faithful God and you empathize with us."

sections.subtitle: Sveti Mihaele, arkanđele, brani nas u boju
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar izgovara molitvu svetom Mihaelu arkanđelu
sections.content:
Odmah nakon molitve oslobođenja Grebenar izgovara tradicionalnu molitvu **svetom Mihaelu arkanđelu**. Ona nastavlja temu duhovne borbe. Arkanđela se moli da brani vjernike „u boju protiv pakosti i zasjeda đavolskih“ i da im bude zaklon.

U središtu molitve je ponizna molba da Bog zapovjedi neprijatelju. Mihael se oslovljava kao **„vojvoda vojske nebeske“**. Od njega se traži da Sotonu i druge zle duhove, „koji svijetom obilaze na propast duša“, božanskom krepošću i jakošću strovali u pakao.

Kratka i sažeta, ova molitva zaokružuje uvodni, zaštitni dio programa prije nego što se molitva usmjeri prema intimnijem odnosu s Isusom i Marijom.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je u skladu s katoličkom vjerom: molitva svetom Mihaelu izražava dopušteno zazivanje anđeoskog zagovora i zaštite, a prikaz duhovne borbe protiv Sotone ima uporište u Svetom pismu i crkvenom nauku. Posebno je primjereno što se pobjeda nad zlom pripisuje Božjoj zapovijedi i snazi, a ne neovisnoj moći arkanđela.
magisterium.enrichment: Otkrivenje 12,7–9 prikazuje Mihaela i njegove anđele u borbi protiv Zmaja, dok Efežanima 6,11–12 govori o kršćanskoj borbi protiv duhovnih sila zla. Katoličko zazivanje svetaca ne znači štovanje koje pripada samo Bogu: moli se za njihovo zagovorništvo i pomoć, dok se konačna obrana i pobjeda pripisuju Bogu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is in accordance with the Catholic faith: the prayer to Saint Michael expresses the permissible invocation of angelic intercession and protection, and the depiction of spiritual warfare against Satan has a foundation in Sacred Scripture and Church teaching. It is especially appropriate that victory over evil is attributed to God's command and power, rather than to an independent power of the archangel.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Revelation 12:7–9 portrays Michael and his angels fighting against the Dragon, while Ephesians 6:11–12 speaks of the Christian struggle against spiritual forces of evil. The Catholic invocation of saints does not mean the worship that belongs to God alone: one prays for their intercession and help, while ultimate defense and victory are attributed to God.

sections.subtitle_en: Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar recites the prayer to Saint Michael the Archangel
sections.content_en:
Immediately after the prayer of deliverance, Grebenar recites the traditional prayer to **Saint Michael the Archangel**. It continues the theme of spiritual warfare. The Archangel is prayed to defend the faithful "in battle against the wickedness and snares of the devil" and to be their protection.

At the center of the prayer is a humble petition that God command the enemy. Michael is addressed as **"prince of the heavenly host"**. He is asked to thrust into hell, by divine power and strength, Satan and other evil spirits "who roam through the world for the ruin of souls."

Short and concise, this prayer rounds off the introductory, protective part of the program before the prayer is directed toward a more intimate relationship with Jesus and Mary.

sections.subtitle: „Neka naša srca kucaju zajedno“: molitva za jedinstvo s Isusom
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj moli nježnu molitvu za jedinstvo s Isusom
sections.content:
Nakon molitava borbe ton se mijenja. Slijedi nježna i osobna molitva upućena „ljupkom Isusu“. Ona izražava čežnju za potpunim jedinstvom s njim i nabraja gotovo cijelo ljudsko biće:

- neka **noge** zajedno hode,
- neka **ruke** budu skupljene u jedinstvu,
- neka **srca** kucaju zajedno,
- neka **duše** budu u skladu,
- neka **misli** budu kao jedno,
- neka **uši** zajedno slušaju tišinu,
- neka **pogledi** duboko prodru jedan u drugi,
- neka **usne** zajedno mole.

Cilj tog jedinstva izražen je u završnoj rečenici: zajednička molitva treba pomoći da se „zadobije milosrđe od vječnoga Oca“. Time se ujedno najavljuje središnja tema ovog molitvenog dijela, a to je Božje milosrđe.

magisterium.assessment: Molitva izražava katolički razumljivu čežnju za zajedništvom s Isusom i za molitvom koja se uzda u milosrđe Oca. Njezine tjelesne slike djeluju poetski i pobožno, a ne kao tvrdnja da vjernici gube svoju osobnost ili doslovno postaju jedno biće s Isusom.
concerns: Izraz da zajednička molitva pomaže „zadobiti” milosrđe mogao bi se pogrešno shvatiti kao da molitva zaslužuje ili prisiljava Boga da udijeli milosrđe; bolje ga je razumjeti kao poniznu molbu i pouzdanje u Božju dobrotu.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusova molitva „da svi budu jedno” (Iv 17,21) pokazuje da kršćansko jedinstvo izvire iz zajedništva s Bogom i treba svjedočiti svijetu. Zajednička molitva jest djelotvorna, ali ne upravlja Božjim odgovorom: jedinstvo je dar milosrđa Oca, kojemu se vjernici ponizno utječu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The prayer expresses a Catholicly understandable longing for communion with Jesus and for prayer that trusts in the mercy of the Father. Its bodily imagery appears poetic and devotional, rather than as an assertion that believers lose their individuality or literally become one being with Jesus.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' prayer „that they may all be one” (Jn 17:21) shows that Christian unity springs from communion with God and ought to witness to the world. Common prayer is efficacious, but it does not direct God's response: unity is a gift of the Father's mercy, to whom believers humbly have recourse.
concerns_en: The expression that common prayer helps to „obtain” mercy could be mistakenly understood as though prayer merits or forces God to grant mercy; it is better understood as a humble request and trust in God's goodness.

sections.subtitle_en: "May our hearts beat together": prayer for unity with Jesus
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host prays a tender prayer for unity with Jesus
sections.content_en:
After the prayers of combat, the tone changes. There follows a tender and personal prayer addressed to "sweet Jesus." It expresses a longing for complete unity with him and enumerates almost the entire human being:

- may our **feet** walk together,
- may our **hands** be joined in unity,
- may our **hearts** beat together,
- may our **souls** be in harmony,
- may our **thoughts** be as one,
- may our **ears** listen to the silence together,
- may our **glances** deeply penetrate one another,
- may our **lips** pray together.

The goal of this unity is expressed in the closing sentence: communal prayer should help to "obtain mercy from the eternal Father." This at the same time announces the central theme of this prayer part, which is the Divine Mercy.

sections.subtitle: Posveta Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu i predanje Presvetom Srcu Isusovu
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar moli posvetu Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu
sections.content:
Sljedeće dvije molitve čine cjelinu predanja. Prva je **posveta Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu**. Molitelj se obraća „Presvetoj Djevici Mariji, majci i kraljici“ i posvećuje joj „čitavo svoje biće, svoje misli, riječi i djela“. Mariji se prepušta da raspolaže sa svime što mu pripada, „sada i u vječnosti“. Svrha je trostruka: hvala i slava Presvetoga Trojstva, posvećenje Crkve i spasenje svega svijeta.

U drugom dijelu posvete molitelj traži pomoć da živi dostojno svoga **krsnog posvećenja** i da „neopozivo pripada svome Otkupitelju“. Moli i da, poput Marije, sluša poticaje Duha Svetoga te da se u njemu i u svemu vrši volja Božja.

Zatim slijedi **molitva Presvetom Srcu Isusovu**, „izvoru svakoga dobra“. Ona počinje klanjanjem, ispoviješću vjere i pouzdanja te kajanjem za grijehe. Molitelj Isusu poklanja svoje „siromašno srce“ i moli da ga učini:

- poniznim,
- strpljivim,
- čistim,
- i u svemu skladnim s Isusovim željama.

Molitva završava nizom konkretnih molbi: da molitelj živi u Isusu i Isus u njemu, da ga štiti u opasnostima i tješi u nevoljama i žalostima, da mu udijeli zdravlje tijela, blagoslovi sav rad i podari **milost svete smrti**. Molba za ponizno srce lijepo se povezuje s uvodnim evanđeljem dana.

magisterium.assessment: Opisane molitve uglavnom su u skladu s katoličkim naukom: marijansko predanje usmjereno je prema vjernosti Bogu i krsnim obećanjima, a molitva Srcu Isusovu izražava pouzdanje u Krista i njegovu milost. Potrebno je samo jasno razumjeti da je „posveta“ Mariji u pobožnom, analognom smislu čin povjeravanja i traženja njezina zagovora, a ne posveta koja bi Mariju postavila na mjesto Boga.
concerns: Izraz da se Mariji predaje „čitavo svoje biće“ i da ona raspolaže svime što molitelju pripada može biti teološki ispravan kao jezik povjeravanja, ali traži jasnoću: konačno se čovjek posvećuje Bogu, po Kristu u Duhu Svetom, uz Marijin zagovor, te se takvim predanjem nastoji vjernije živjeti krsne obveze.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni Direktorij potiče marijansko povjeravanje kao način življenja krsnog predanja, ali upozorava da se izraz „posveta Mariji“ upotrebljava analogno i da ne znači isto što i liturgijska posveta Bogu. Ivan Pavao II. opisuje Marijinu ulogu kao pomoć u prikazivanju sebe i čovječanstva Bogu, kroz otkupiteljsku žrtvu Krista; zato su predanje Mariji i pripadnost Kristu međusobno usmjereni, a ne suprotstavljeni.

magisterium.assessment_en: The described prayers are mainly in accordance with Catholic teaching: Marian surrender is directed toward fidelity to God and baptismal promises, and the prayer to the Heart of Jesus expresses trust in Christ and his grace. It is only necessary to understand clearly that „consecration” to Mary in a devotional, analogous sense is an act of entrustment and seeking her intercession, not a consecration that would put Mary in the place of God.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church's Directory encourages Marian entrustment as a way of living out baptismal dedication, but cautions that the term „consecration to Mary” is used analogously and does not mean the same as liturgical consecration to God. John Paul II describes Mary's role as helping in offering oneself and humanity to God, through the redemptive sacrifice of Christ; therefore, surrender to Mary and belonging to Christ are mutually directed, not opposed.
concerns_en: The expression that „one's entire being” is surrendered to Mary and that she disposes of everything belonging to the person praying can be theologically correct as language of entrustment, but requires clarity: ultimately man is consecrated to God, through Christ in the Holy Spirit, with Mary's intercession, and such surrender seeks to live baptismal obligations more faithfully.

sections.subtitle_en: Consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary and surrender to the Sacred Heart of Jesus
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar prays the consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary
sections.content_en:
The following two prayers form a whole of surrender. The first is the **consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary**. The pray-er addresses the "Blessed Virgin Mary, mother and queen" and consecrates to her "one's entire being, one's thoughts, words, and deeds." Mary is left to dispose of everything that belongs to him, "now and in eternity." The purpose is threefold: the praise and glory of the Most Holy Trinity, the sanctification of the Church, and the salvation of the whole world.

In the second part of the consecration, the pray-er asks for help to live worthily of his **baptismal consecration** and to "belong irrevocably to his Redeemer." He also prays that, like Mary, he may listen to the promptings of the Holy Spirit and that the will of God may be done in him and in everything.

Then follows the **prayer to the Sacred Heart of Jesus**, "the source of every good." It begins with adoration, confession of faith and trust, and contrition for sins. The pray-er gives his "poor heart" to Jesus and prays that he make it:

- humble,
- patient,
- pure,
- and in everything in harmony with Jesus' desires.

The prayer ends with a series of concrete petitions: that the pray-er may live in Jesus and Jesus in him, that he protect him in dangers and comfort him in troubles and sorrows, that he grant him health of body, bless all work, and bestow the **grace of a holy death**. The petition for a humble heart ties in nicely with the opening gospel of the day.

sections.subtitle: Krunica Božjega milosrđa: „Po njegovoj pregorkoj muci, budi milosrdan nama i cijelome svijetu“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj predvodi Krunicu Božjega milosrđa, molitva „Vječni Oče, prikazujemo ti…“
sections.content:
U 00:03:45 Vladimir Grebenar najavljuje **Krunicu Božjega milosrđa**, središnji dio molitvenog programa u epizodi naslovljenoj „Milosrđe Božje“. Krunica počinje trima temeljnim molitvama:

- **Oče naš**,
- **Zdravo Marijo**,
- **Vjerovanje** („Vjerujem u Boga Oca svemogućega…“), u kojem se ispovijeda vjera u Krista začetog po Duhu Svetom, rođenog od Marije Djevice i mučenog pod Poncijem Pilatom, te u svetu Crkvu katoličku, općinstvo svetih, oproštenje grijeha, uskrsnuće tijela i život vječni.

Srž krunice čini prikazanje Ocu, koje se ponavlja na početku svakog desetka:

> „Vječni Oče, prikazujemo ti tijelo i krv, dušu i božanstvo preljubljenoga Sina tvojega, Gospodina našega Isusa Krista, kao zadovoljštinu za grijehe naše i cijeloga svijeta.“

Nakon prikazanja slijedi niz ponovljenih zaziva: **„Po njegovoj pregorkoj muci, budi milosrdan nama i cijelome svijetu.“** Grebenar ih izgovara mirnim, ujednačenim ritmom. Ponavljanje prožima gotovo osam minuta snimke i stvara meditativno ozračje.

Ovakav način molitve naglašava poruku zajedništva. Moli se milosrđe ne samo za pojedinca, nego „nama i cijelome svijetu“. Isusova muka pritom se predstavlja kao temelj na kojem se svaka molba za oproštenje i smilovanje oslanja.

magisterium.assessment: Opis Krunice Božjega milosrđa u bitnome je usklađen s katoličkom vjerom: molitva se obraća Ocu, oslanja se na Kristovu muku i moli milosrđe za molitelje i cijeli svijet. Govor o prikazanju Kristova tijela i krvi kao zadovoljštini ispravno se razumije kao molitveno sjedinjenje s jedinstvenom Kristovom žrtvom, a ne kao njezino ponavljanje ili nadopunjavanje.
magisterium.enrichment: Molitva za „nas i cijeli svijet“ izražava široki, zajedničarski horizont Božjega milosrđa, a Kristova muka nije odvojena od ljubavi Oca i Sina koja donosi spasenje. Crkveno učenje razlikuje Kristovu jednokratnu krvavu žrtvu na križu od njezina sakramentalnog uprisutnjenja u euharistiji; molitva Krunice Božjega milosrđa upućuje na tu žrtvu i sjedinjuje vjernike s njom, ali nije sama euharistijska žrtva.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the Chaplet of the Divine Mercy is essentially aligned with the Catholic faith: the prayer addresses the Father, relies on Christ's Passion, and begs mercy for the persons praying and the whole world. Speaking of offering Christ's Body and Blood as satisfaction is correctly understood as prayerful union with Christ's unique sacrifice, not as its repetition or completion.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Praying for „us and the whole world” expresses the broad, communal horizon of God's mercy, and Christ's Passion is not separated from the love of the Father and the Son which brings salvation. Church teaching distinguishes Christ's once-for-all bloody sacrifice on the Cross from its sacramental representation in the Eucharist; the prayer of the Chaplet of the Divine Mercy points to that sacrifice and unites believers with it, but is not itself the Eucharistic sacrifice.

sections.subtitle_en: Chaplet of the Divine Mercy: "For the sake of His sorrowful Passion, have mercy on us and on the whole world"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host leads the Chaplet of the Divine Mercy, prayer "Eternal Father, we offer you…"
sections.content_en:
At 00:03:45 Vladimir Grebenar announces the **Chaplet of the Divine Mercy**, the central part of the prayer program in the episode titled "The Divine Mercy." The Chaplet begins with three basic prayers:

- **Our Father**,
- **Hail Mary**,
- **Creed** ("I believe in God the Father almighty…"), in which faith is confessed in Christ conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary, and suffered under Pontius Pilate, and in the holy Catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and life everlasting.

The core of the chaplet consists of the offering to the Father, which is repeated at the beginning of each decade:

> "Eternal Father, we offer you the body and blood, soul and divinity of your dearly beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, in atonement for our sins and those of the whole world."

After the offering follows a series of repeated invocations: **"For the sake of His sorrowful Passion, have mercy on us and on the whole world."** Grebenar recites them in a calm, steady rhythm. The repetition permeates almost eight minutes of the recording and creates a meditative atmosphere.

This manner of praying emphasizes the message of communion. Mercy is prayed for not only for the individual, but "on us and on the whole world." Jesus' passion is presented here as the foundation on which every petition for forgiveness and mercy rests.

sections.subtitle: „Sveti Bože, sveti jaki Bože“ i trostruko „Isuse, uzdam se u tebe“
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar završava krunicu trostrukim „Isuse, uzdam se u tebe“
sections.content:
Završetak Krunice Božjega milosrđa u 00:11:38 donosi drugačiji ritam. Grebenar tri puta izgovara drevni zaziv:

> „Sveti Bože, sveti jaki Bože, sveti besmrtni Bože, smiluj se nama i cijelome svijetu.“

Slijedi zaziv koji Isusovo srce prikazuje kao izvor milosrđa: „O krvi i vodo, što potekoste iz srca Isusova, kao izvor milosrđa za nas, uzdam se u tebe.“ Zatim se zaziva i Marija kao **majka milosrđa**, s molbom da moli za vjernike.

Vrhunac čini trostruko ponovljena kratka molitva pouzdanja: **„Isuse, uzdam se u tebe.“** Ona u sažetom obliku izražava cijelu duhovnost Božjeg milosrđa. Krunica se zaključuje molbom: „Smiluj se nama i cijelomu svijetu, Gospodine.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je u skladu s katoličkim naukom: pouzdanje u Isusa, zazivanje Božjeg milosrđa i Marijino zagovorništvo prikazani su kao molitva, a ne kao zamjena za Kristovo otkupiteljsko djelo. Krv i voda iz Kristova boka te zaziv „Isuse, uzdam se u tebe“ odgovaraju katoličkoj pobožnosti Božjem milosrđu.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva povezuje ovu pobožnost s Kristovom smrću i uskrsnućem, iz kojih izvire milosrđe što oprašta grijehe i vraća radost spasenja; zato je treba razumjeti u svjetlu uskrsnog otajstva i liturgije. Ivan Pavao II. povezao je Kristov probodeni bok s krvlju i vodom te potvrdio zazivanje Marije kao „Majke milosrđa“ i molitvu „Isuse, uzdam se u tebe“.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is in accordance with Catholic teaching: trust in Jesus, the invocation of God's mercy, and Mary's intercession are presented as prayer, rather than as a substitute for Christ's redemptive work. The blood and water from Christ's side and the invocation „Jesus, I trust in you” correspond to Catholic devotion to the Divine Mercy.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church connects this devotion with Christ's Death and Resurrection, from which springs the mercy that forgives sins and restores the joy of salvation; therefore, it should be understood in the light of the Paschal mystery and the liturgy. John Paul II connected Christ's pierced side with blood and water and affirmed the invocation of Mary as „Mother of Mercy” and the prayer „Jesus, I trust in you”.

sections.subtitle_en: "Holy God, Holy Mighty One" and the threefold "Jesus, I trust in you"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar finishes the chaplet with the threefold "Jesus, I trust in you"
sections.content_en:
The conclusion of the Chaplet of the Divine Mercy at 00:11:38 brings a different rhythm. Grebenar recites the ancient invocation three times:

> "Holy God, Holy Mighty One, Holy Immortal One, have mercy on us and on the whole world."

There follows an invocation presenting the heart of Jesus as the fountain of mercy: "O blood and water, which gushed forth from the heart of Jesus as a fount of mercy for us, I trust in you." Then Mary is also invoked as **mother of mercy**, with a petition that she pray for the faithful.

The climax is formed by the threefold repeated short prayer of trust: **"Jesus, I trust in you."** In summary form, it expresses the entire spirituality of the Divine Mercy. The Chaplet concludes with the petition: "Have mercy on us and on the whole world, Lord."

sections.subtitle: Litanije Božjem milosrđu: od tajne Trojstva do utjehe umirućih
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj moli Litanije Božjem milosrđu, zaziv „Milosrđe Božje, ti neshvatljiva tajno Presvetoga Trojstva“
sections.content:
U 00:12:27 slijede **Litanije Božjem milosrđu**. Počinju uobičajenim litanijskim uvodom: „Gospodine, smiluj se. Kriste, smiluj se“, a zatim i zazivima Ocu nebeskom, Sinu Otkupitelju svijeta, Duhu Svetom i Svetom Trojstvu, jednom Bogu.

Svaki sljedeći zaziv počinje riječima „Milosrđe Božje“ i završava odgovorom **„uzdam se u tebe“**. Zazivi zajedno daju gotovo teološki pregled djelovanja Božjeg milosrđa kroz povijest spasenja i ljudski život. Milosrđe se zaziva kao:

- **neshvatljiva tajna Presvetoga Trojstva** i izraz njegove najveće moći,
- milosrđe koje se objavilo u **stvaranju nebeskih duhova** i koje je ljude **iz ništavila pozvalo u život**,
- milosrđe koje obuhvaća čitav svijet i daruje besmrtan život,
- zaštita od zasluženih kazni i oslobođenje od bijede grijeha,
- milosrđe koje se izlijeva **iz rana Kristovih** i izvire iz Presvetoga Srca,
- milosrđe koje je ljudima darovalo **Presvetu Djevicu za majku milosrđa**,
- milosrđe vidljivo u **ustanovljenju Crkve** te u ustanovljenju i dijeljenju sakramenata,
- milosrđe „neograničeno u sakramentu krštenja i pokore“ i „neizmjerno u sakramentu oltara i svećeništva“,
- milosrđe koje poziva k svetoj vjeri, obraća grešnike, posvećuje pravednike i usavršava svete,
- **vrelo bolesnicima i patnicima**, utjeha onih koji su skršena srca i ufanje onih koji očajavaju,
- **mir umirućih**, zaštita od paklenoga ognja i olakšanje patnji dušama u čistilištu,
- slast i neizmjerna radost svih svetih, beskrajno u svim tajnama vjere i neiscrpan izvor čudesa.

Litanije završavaju psalmskim retkom: „Bog je milosrdan i pun samilosti, spor na srđbu i pun dobrote. Zato ću dovijeka klicati milosrđu Božjemu.“

magisterium.assessment: Opisane Litanije Božjem milosrđu uglavnom su usklađene s katoličkom vjerom jer usmjeravaju pouzdanje prema Bogu, čije se milosrđe objavljuje u Kristu i djeluje u životu Crkve. Formulacije o zaštiti od kazne, paklenom ognju i olakšanju patnji duša u čistilištu treba razumjeti kao molitvene prošnje, a ne kao automatsko jamstvo da će posljedice grijeha ili Božji sud biti uklonjeni.
concerns: Izraz da milosrđe štiti od zasluženih kazni mogao bi se, ako se izdvoji iz molitvenoga i pokorničkog konteksta, pogrešno protumačiti kao obećanje nekažnjivosti; odlomak ne kaže izričito da je riječ o prošnji.
Dostupni izvori potvrđuju širi kristološki i uskrsni temelj pobožnosti, ali ne potvrđuju pojedinačno sve navedene zazive Litanija niti objašnjavaju svaki od njih.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje Božjeg milosrđa nije odvojeno od obraćenja i oproštenja grijeha: crkvena molitva pouzdano zaziva milosrđe koje može preobraziti čovjeka, a Krist je njegova konačna objava u smrti i uskrsnuću. Takav okvir pomaže čitati zazive o sakramentima, umirućima i pokojnicima kao prošnje Bogu, a ne kao tvrdnju da pobožna formula sama po sebi jamči određeni ishod.

magisterium.assessment_en: The described Litany of the Divine Mercy is mainly aligned with the Catholic faith because it directs trust toward God, whose mercy is revealed in Christ and is active in the life of the Church. Formulations about protection from punishment, hellfire, and easing the suffering of souls in purgatory should be understood as prayerful petitions, rather than as an automatic guarantee that the consequences of sin or God's judgment will be removed.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of God's mercy is not separated from conversion and the forgiveness of sins: Church prayer trustfully invokes mercy that can transform a person, and Christ is its definitive revelation in death and resurrection. Such a framework helps read invocations about the sacraments, the dying, and the deceased as petitions to God, rather than as a claim that a pious formula in itself guarantees a particular outcome.
concerns_en: The expression that mercy protects from deserved punishments could, if isolated from the prayerful and penitential context, be mistakenly interpreted as a promise of impunity; the passage does not explicitly say that it is a petition.
Available sources confirm the broader Christological and Paschal foundation of the devotion, but do not confirm individually all the listed invocations of the Litany nor explain each of them.

sections.subtitle_en: Litany of the Divine Mercy: from the mystery of the Trinity to the consolation of the dying
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host prays the Litany of the Divine Mercy, invocation "Divine Mercy, you incomprehensible mystery of the Most Holy Trinity"
sections.content_en:
At 00:12:27 follows the **Litany of the Divine Mercy**. It begins with the usual litany introduction: "Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy", and then with invocations to the heavenly Father, the Son Redeemer of the world, the Holy Spirit, and the Holy Trinity, one God.

Every subsequent invocation begins with the words "Divine Mercy" and ends with the response **"I trust in you"**. Together, the invocations give almost a theological overview of the action of God's mercy through salvation history and human life. Mercy is invoked as:

- **incomprehensible mystery of the Most Holy Trinity** and expression of its greatest power,
- mercy that was revealed in the **creation of the heavenly spirits** and that called humans **out of nothingness into life**,
- mercy that embraces the entire world and bestows immortal life,
- protection from deserved punishments and liberation from the misery of sin,
- mercy that pours out **from the wounds of Christ** and flows from the Sacred Heart,
- mercy that granted human beings the **Blessed Virgin as mother of mercy**,
- mercy visible in the **institution of the Church** and in the institution and administration of the sacraments,
- mercy "unlimited in the sacrament of baptism and penance" and "immense in the sacrament of the altar and the priesthood",
- mercy that calls to the holy faith, converts sinners, sanctifies the righteous, and perfects the saints,
- **fount for the sick and suffering**, consolation of those who are brokenhearted and hope of those who despair,
- **peace of the dying**, protection from hellfire and relief of sufferings for the souls in purgatory,
- delight and immense joy of all the saints, boundless in all mysteries of faith and an inexhaustible source of miracles.

The litany ends with a psalm verse: "The Lord is gracious and full of compassion, slow to anger and of great mercy. Therefore I will sing of the mercies of the Lord forever."

sections.subtitle: Da u teškim trenucima ne očajavamo: završna molitva pouzdanja
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar izgovara završnu molitvu „Pomolimo se. O vječni Bože…“
sections.content:
Litanije zaključuje svečana molitva koju Grebenar uvodi riječju „Pomolimo se“. Upućena je vječnom Bogu, „čije je milosrđe neistraživo i čije blago smilovanja neiscrpivo“.

U njoj se moli da Bog umnoži svoje milosrđe u vjernicima. Svrha je izrazito pastoralna: **„da u teškim trenucima ne očajavamo i ne budemo obeshrabreni“**. Vjernici se trebaju s velikim pouzdanjem predati Božjoj svetoj volji, „koja je sama ljubav i smilovanje“.

Molitva završava po Isusu Kristu, koji se ovdje naziva **„kraljem milosrđa“** i koji s Ocem i Duhom Svetim „iskazuje milosrđe u sve vijeke vjekova“. Time se zaokružuje cjelina posvećena Božjem milosrđu. Predanje Božjoj volji pritom se nadovezuje na ranije molitve posvete, u kojima se molilo da se „u svemu vrši volja Božja“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je u skladu s katoličkim naukom: pouzdanje u Božje milosrđe i predanje njegovoj volji mogu poduprijeti vjernika u kušnjama, a zaziv Isusa kao kralja milosrđa ne umanjuje njegovu božansku narav. Naglasak na pouzdanju ne znači da kršćanin nikada ne osjeća tjeskobu, nego da se ni u tami očaja ne smatra napuštenim od Boga.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko pouzdanje nije uvjerenje da će svaka teškoća odmah nestati, nego oslonac na Boga koji je blizu, oprašta i vodi čovjeka prema vječnom životu. Božje se milosrđe ne suprotstavlja njegovoj pravednosti: crkveni nauk opisuje ga kao izraz Božje ljubavi i svemoći, a ne kao ravnodušnost prema zlu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is in accordance with Catholic teaching: trust in God's mercy and surrender to his will can sustain the believer in trials, and invoking Jesus as the king of mercy does not diminish his divine nature. The emphasis on trust does not mean that a Christian never feels anxiety, but that even in the darkness of despair one does not consider oneself abandoned by God.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic trust is not a conviction that every difficulty will immediately vanish, but reliance on God who is near, forgives, and guides man toward eternal life. God's mercy is not opposed to his justice: Church teaching describes it as an expression of God's love and omnipotence, rather than as indifference toward evil.

sections.content_en:
The litany is concluded by a solemn prayer that Grebenar introduces with the word "Let us pray." It is addressed to the eternal God, "whose mercy is unfathomable and whose treasure of compassion is inexhaustible."

In it, prayer is made that God multiply his mercy in the faithful. The purpose is distinctly pastoral: **"that in difficult moments we may not despair and not be despondent"**. The faithful should surrender themselves with great trust to God's holy will, "which is love and mercy itself."

The prayer ends through Jesus Christ, who is here called the **"king of mercy"** and who with the Father and the Holy Spirit "shows mercy forever and ever." This rounds off the whole part dedicated to the Divine Mercy. Surrender to God's will thereby connects to earlier prayers of consecration, in which it was prayed that "the will of God be done in everything."

sections.subtitle: Gospina krunica: radosna otajstva od začeća do pohoda Elizabeti
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj najavljuje Gospinu krunicu i prvo otajstvo
sections.content:
Kratkom najavom „Slijedi Gospina krunica“ Vladimir Grebenar u 00:16:50 započinje drugi veliki molitveni ciklus, a to su **radosna otajstva**. Svaki desetak ima istu strukturu:

- najava otajstva,
- **Oče naš**,
- deset puta **Zdravo Marijo**,
- **Slava Ocu**,
- molitva **„O moj Isuse, oprosti nam naše grijehe, očuvaj nas od paklenoga ognja, dovedi u raj sve duše, a osobito one kojima je najpotrebnije tvoje milosrđe.“**

Završna molitva svakog desetka ponovno ističe temu milosrđa, koja povezuje Gospinu krunicu s prethodnom Krunicom Božjega milosrđa.

**Prvo otajstvo**, najavljeno u 00:16:53, glasi: „koga si, Djevice, po Duhu Svetom začela“. Ono razmatra trenutak utjelovljenja i Marijin pristanak Božjem planu.

**Drugo otajstvo** slijedi u 00:20:51: „koga si, Djevice, idući Elizabeti u pohode nosila“. Ono prati Mariju na putu prema rođakinji Elizabeti dok u sebi nosi Isusa. Oba desetka Grebenar moli istim smirenim, ujednačenim ritmom.

magisterium.assessment: Opis radosnih otajstava i molitvenog obrasca Gospine krunice u bitnome je usklađen s katoličkom vjerom: prvo otajstvo upućuje na začeće Isusa po Duhu Svetom, a drugo na Marijin pohod Elizabeti. Takvo razmatranje usmjerava pozornost na Krista i utjelovljenje, dok se Marijin pristanak prikazuje kao odgovor vjere na Božji plan.
magisterium.enrichment: Luka izvještava da je Marija pristala na anđelovu riječ, da je Duh Sveti sišao na nju te da je Elizabeta naziva majkom Gospodina; Ivan u njezinoj utrobi zaigrao je od radosti. Zato su ova otajstva istodobno marijanska i kristocentrična: Marija vodi razmatranje prema Isusu, utjelovljenom Sinu i Spasitelju.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the joyful mysteries and the prayer formula of the Holy Rosary is essentially aligned with the Catholic faith: the first mystery points to the conception of Jesus by the Holy Spirit, and the second to Mary's visitation to Elizabeth. Such meditation directs attention to Christ and the Incarnation, while Mary's consent is presented as a response of faith to God's plan.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Luke reports that Mary consented to the angel's word, that the Holy Spirit came upon her, and that Elizabeth calls her the mother of the Lord; John leaped for joy in her womb. Therefore, these mysteries are simultaneously Marian and Christocentric: Mary leads meditation toward Jesus, the incarnate Son and Savior.

sections.subtitle_en: The Rosary of Our Lady: joyful mysteries from the conception to the visitation to Elizabeth
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host announces the Rosary of Our Lady and the first mystery
sections.content_en:
With the short announcement "The Rosary of Our Lady follows," Vladimir Grebenar at 00:16:50 begins the second large prayer cycle, which is the **joyful mysteries**. Each decade has the same structure:

- announcement of the mystery,
- **Our Father**,
- ten times **Hail Mary**,
- **Glory Be**,
- prayer **"O my Jesus, forgive us our sins, save us from the fires of hell, lead all souls to heaven, especially those in most need of your mercy."**

The closing prayer of each decade highlights once again the theme of mercy, which links the Rosary of Our Lady to the preceding Chaplet of the Divine Mercy.

The **first mystery**, announced at 00:16:53, reads: "whom you, O Virgin, conceived by the Holy Spirit." It contemplates the moment of the incarnation and Mary's consent to God's plan.

The **second mystery** follows at 00:20:51: "whom you, O Virgin, bore in visitation to Elizabeth." It follows Mary on the way to her relative Elizabeth while carrying Jesus within herself. Grebenar prays both decades with the same calm, steady rhythm.

sections.subtitle: Rođenje, prikazanje i pronalazak u hramu: dovršetak radosnih otajstava
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar najavljuje četvrto otajstvo: „koga si, Djevice, u hramu prikazala“
sections.content:
Krunica se nastavlja trećim, četvrtim i petim radosnim otajstvom. Sva tri prate Isusovo djetinjstvo:

- **Treće otajstvo** (00:24:53): „koga si, Djevica, rodila“. Razmatra se rođenje Isusovo.
- **Četvrto otajstvo** (00:29:03): „koga si, Djevice, u hramu prikazala“. Razmatra se prikazanje Isusa u hramu.
- **Peto otajstvo** (00:32:56): „koga si, Djevice, u hramu našla“. Razmatra se trenutak kada Marija pronalazi Isusa u hramu.

Prije najave petog otajstva nastupa nešto duža stanka, nakon čega molitva teče dalje istim redoslijedom. Svaki desetak završava doksologijom „Slava Ocu i Sinu i Duhu Svetomu. Kako bijaše na početku, tako i sada i vazda i u vijeke vjekova. Amen“ i molitvom „O moj Isuse“, u kojoj se moli oproštenje grijeha i spasenje duša kojima je Božje milosrđe najpotrebnije.

Radosna otajstva tako prolaze kroz Isusovo djetinjstvo, od Marijina začeća po Duhu Svetom do pronalaska dječaka Isusa u hramu.

magisterium.assessment: Opis trećeg, četvrtog i petog radosnog otajstva u skladu je s katoličkom predajom krunice i evanđeoskim događajima Isusova rođenja, prikazanja u hramu i pronalaska u hramu. Jedina važna nejasnoća jest završna formulacija „od Marijina začeća po Duhu Svetom“, koja se može pogrešno razumjeti kao da je Marija začeta po Duhu Svetom, umjesto da je Isus začet u Marijinoj utrobi djelovanjem Duha Svetoga.
concerns: Radi doktrinarne jasnoće trebalo bi reći „od Isusova začeća u Marijinoj utrobi po Duhu Svetom“: kršćanska vjera ispovijeda da je Isus začet po Duhu Svetom, a ne da je Marija tako začeta.
magisterium.enrichment: Ivan Pavao II. potvrđuje da radosna otajstva obuhvaćaju i prikazanje i pronalazak Isusa u hramu te ističe da se u posljednjim otajstvima radost već isprepliće s dramom koja najavljuje Kristovu muku. U molitvi krunice razmatranje tih prizora usmjerava vjernika prema Kristu, a ne samo prema događajima Isusova djetinjstva.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the third, fourth, and fifth joyful mysteries is in accordance with the Catholic tradition of the Rosary and the evangelical events of Jesus' Nativity, the Presentation in the Temple, and the Finding in the Temple. The only important ambiguity is the concluding formulation „from Mary's conception by the Holy Spirit”, which can be mistakenly understood as though Mary was conceived by the Holy Spirit, rather than that Jesus was conceived in Mary's womb by the action of the Holy Spirit.
magisterium.enrichment_en: John Paul II confirms that the joyful mysteries encompass both the Presentation and the Finding of Jesus in the Temple, and emphasizes that in the last mysteries joy is already intertwined with drama foreshadowing Christ's Passion. In the prayer of the Rosary, meditation on these scenes directs the believer toward Christ, and not only toward the events of Jesus' childhood.
concerns_en: For the sake of doctrinal clarity, one should say „from Jesus' conception in Mary's womb by the Holy Spirit”: the Christian faith professes that Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit, not that Mary was conceived in this way.

sections.subtitle_en: Nativity, presentation, and finding in the temple: completion of the joyful mysteries
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar announces the fourth mystery: "whom you, O Virgin, presented in the temple"
sections.content_en:
The Rosary continues with the third, fourth, and fifth joyful mysteries. All three follow Jesus' childhood:

- **Third mystery** (00:24:53): "whom you, O Virgin, brought forth." The birth of Jesus is contemplated.
- **Fourth mystery** (00:29:03): "whom you, O Virgin, presented in the temple." The presentation of Jesus in the temple is contemplated.
- **Fifth mystery** (00:32:56): "whom you, O Virgin, found in the temple." The moment when Mary finds Jesus in the temple is contemplated.

Before the announcement of the fifth mystery, a slightly longer pause occurs, after which the prayer flows further in the same order. Each decade ends with the doxology "Glory be to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen" and the prayer "O my Jesus," in which forgiveness of sins and the salvation of souls who most need God's mercy are implored.

The joyful mysteries thus move through Jesus' childhood, from Mary's conception by the Holy Spirit to the finding of the boy Jesus in the temple.

sections.subtitle: „Zdravo Kraljice, majko milosrđa“: završni pozdrav Djevici
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj zaključuje molitveni dio molitvom „Zdravo Kraljice“
sections.content:
Molitveni dio završava u 00:37:01 molitvom **„Zdravo Kraljice“**. Marija se u njoj ponovno oslovljava kao **„majka milosrđa“**, čime se vraća glavna tema epizode. Naziva se i „život, slast i ufanje naše“.

Molitva slikovito opisuje ljudsko stanje. Vjernici su „prognani sinovi Jevini“ koji Mariji vapiju i uzdišu „tugujući i plačući u ovoj suznoj dolini“. Mariju, „zagovornicu“, mole da na njih svrne svoje milostive oči te da im „poslije ovoga progona“ pokaže Isusa, „blagoslovljeni plod utrobe svoje“.

Molitva završava nježnim trostrukim zazivom: **„O blaga, o mila, o slatka Djevice Marijo. Amen.“** Time se zatvara više od pola sata neprekinute molitve. Ona je započela vezivanjem zlih sila i zaštitom obitelji, a završava predanjem pod okrilje Marije kao majke milosrđa.

magisterium.assessment: Opis molitve „Zdravo Kraljice“ u skladu je s katoličkom marijanskom pobožnošću: Mariju se zaziva kao majku i zagovornicu, dok se od nje moli da vjernike usmjeri prema Isusu, a ne da zauzme njegovo mjesto. Izraz „poslije ovoga progona“ može biti manje precizan od tradicionalnog značenja „poslije ovoga progonstva“ ili „izgnanstva“, koje označava zemaljsko putovanje i stanje čovjeka, a ne nužno progon u užem smislu.
concerns: Izraz „poslije ovoga progona“ može zvučati kao da se misli samo na vanjsko progonstvo; tradicionalni smisao zaziva jest da se od Marije traži da nam nakon zemaljskog izgnanstva pokaže Isusa.
magisterium.enrichment: Marijanski karakter krunice nije suprotstavljen njezinu kristološkom središtu: papa Ivan Pavao II. ističe da se u zazivu Marijina zagovora vjernik pouzdaje u njezino majčinsko posredovanje, a istodobno ostaje usmjeren prema Kristu i njegovu spasenju. Zato se Mariju može nazivati majkom milosrđa i zagovornicom, a da se Božje milosrđe i Kristovo jedinstveno spasenjsko poslanje ne pripisuju njoj kao izvoru neovisnom o Bogu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the prayer „Hail, Holy Queen” is in accordance with Catholic Marian devotion: Mary is invoked as mother and advocate, while she is asked to direct believers toward Jesus, rather than take his place. The expression „after this persecution” can be less precise than the traditional meaning of „after this exile” or „banishment”, which denotes the earthly journey and condition of man, rather than necessarily persecution in the narrower sense.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Marian character of the Rosary is not opposed to its Christological center: Pope John Paul II emphasizes that in invoking Mary's intercession the believer relies on her maternal mediation, while at the same time remaining directed toward Christ and his salvation. Therefore, Mary can be called mother of mercy and advocate, without attributing God's mercy and Christ's unique salvific mission to her as a source independent of God.
concerns_en: The expression „after this persecution” can sound as though only external persecution is meant; the traditional sense of the invocation is asking Mary to show us Jesus after our earthly exile.

sections.subtitle_en: "Hail, Holy Queen, Mother of Mercy": closing greeting to the Virgin
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host concludes the prayer part with the prayer "Hail, Holy Queen"
sections.content_en:
The prayer part ends at 00:37:01 with the prayer **"Hail, Holy Queen"**. In it, Mary is again addressed as **"Mother of Mercy"**, which brings back the main theme of the episode. She is also called "our life, our sweetness, and our hope."

The prayer vividly describes the human condition. The faithful are "poor banished children of Eve" who cry and sigh to Mary, "mourning and weeping in this valley of tears." They ask Mary, their "advocate," to turn her eyes of mercy toward them and, "after this exile," show unto them Jesus, "the blessed fruit of thy womb."

The prayer ends with a tender threefold invocation: **"O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary. Amen."** This concludes more than half an hour of uninterrupted prayer. It began with the binding of evil forces and the protection of families, and ends with surrender under the mantle of Mary as mother of mercy.

sections.subtitle: „Meni je živjeti Krist, a umrijeti dobitak“: Pavlova radost usred okova
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar započinje čitanje iz Poslanice Filipljanima
sections.content:
Nakon zajedničke molitve krunice i pozdrava Zdravo Kraljice, voditelj emisije **Vladimir Grebenar** prelazi na središnji dio susreta, tumačenje svete riječi. Za početak čita odlomak iz **Poslanice Filipljanima**, tekst koji će obilježiti cijelo razmatranje.

U čitanju sveti Pavao piše: „Braćo, samo neka se na svaki način, bilo himbeno, bilo istinito, Krist navješćuje, i tome se radujem, a i radovat ću se.“ Apostol nastavlja da se nada kako se ni zbog čega neće smesti te da će se Krist uzveličati u njegovu tijelu, bilo životom bilo smrću. Iz toga proizlazi i čuvena rečenica: **„Meni je živjeti Krist, a umrijeti dobitak.“**

Grebenar čita i Pavlovu unutarnju dvojbu. Apostol se osjeća pritiješnjenim između dvije mogućnosti. S jedne strane želi otići i biti s Kristom, „jer to je mnogo, mnogo bolje“. S druge strane, ostati u tijelu „potrebnije je poradi vas“, za napredak i radost vjere zajednice kojoj piše. Upravo će prva rečenica tog odlomka, Pavlova radost što se Krist navješćuje, postati ključ cijelog tumačenja.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak vjerno prenosi Fil 1,15–26: Pavao se raduje što se Krist navješćuje čak i kada neki propovijedaju iz neiskrenih motiva, te želi da se Krist proslavi u njegovu tijelu bilo životom bilo smrću. Njegova želja da bude s Kristom ne poništava vrijednost zemaljskog života, jer ostanak smatra potrebnim za rast i radost vjere zajednice.
magisterium.enrichment: Izraz „meni je živjeti Krist, a umrijeti dobitak” ne znači da Pavao smatra život bezvrijednim: život mu je plodan jer služi Kristu i bližnjima, dok smrt vidi kao odlazak da bude s Kristom. Benedikt XVI. ističe kako se Pavlova sloboda pred smrću povezuje sa spremnošću da nastavi živjeti za druge i izvršiti Božju volju.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage faithfully conveys Phil 1:15–26: Paul rejoices that Christ is proclaimed even when some preach from insincere motives, and desires that Christ be glorified in his body whether by life or by death. His desire to be with Christ does not negate the value of earthly life, because he considers remaining necessary for the growth and joy of faith of the community.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The expression „for to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain” does not mean that Paul considers life worthless: his life is fruitful because he serves Christ and his neighbors, while he sees death as departing to be with Christ. Benedict XVI highlights how Paul's freedom in the face of death is connected with readiness to continue living for others and to fulfill God's will.

sections.subtitle_en: "For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain": Paul's joy in the midst of chains
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar begins reading from the Epistle to the Philippians
sections.content_en:
After communal prayer of the rosary and the Hail, Holy Queen greeting, the host of the show, **Vladimir Grebenar**, moves to the central part of the gathering, the interpretation of the holy word. To begin, he reads a passage from the **Epistle to the Philippians**, a text that will mark the entire reflection.

In the reading, Saint Paul writes: "Brethren, only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed, and in that I rejoice, yes, and I will rejoice." The apostle continues that he hopes he will in no way be confounded, and that Christ will be magnified in his body, whether by life or by death. From this comes the famous sentence: **"For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain."**

Grebenar also reads Paul's inner dilemma. The apostle feels hard-pressed between two possibilities. On the one hand, he desires to depart and be with Christ, "for that is far, far better." On the other hand, to remain in the flesh is "more necessary for your sake," for the progress and joy of faith of the community to which he writes. It is precisely the first sentence of that passage, Paul's joy that Christ is proclaimed, that will become the key to the entire interpretation.

sections.subtitle: Tajna Pavlova uspjeha: radovao se tuđem navještaju
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava zašto je sveti Pavao bio uspješan u evangelizaciji
sections.content:
Tumačeći pročitano, Vladimir Grebenar najprije pojašnjava izraz „himbeno“. Prema njegovim riječima, riječ je o navještaju koji dolazi „s nekim interesom, ne onako iz srca“. Pavlu je ipak važno samo to da se Isus navješćuje, a tome se raduje i radovat će se.

U tome voditelj vidi **odgovor na pitanje zašto je Pavao bio toliko uspješan u evangelizaciji**: radovao se što drugi navješćuju Krista. Zatim slušatelje poziva da zamisle Isusa, raspetoga Spasitelja, kako se raduje kada ga ljudi navješćuju, pronose njegovo ime po svijetu, ne zataje ga, svjedoče za njega, hvale ga i slave.

### Otac stolar i sin koji ga nadmaši

Kako bi to približio, Grebenar se služi slikom iz svakodnevnog života. Svaki se roditelj raduje kad njegovo dijete uspije u nečemu čemu ga je on poučio. Kao primjer navodi oca poduzetnika, stolara, koji sina nauči zanatu. Takav se otac raduje kad vidi da sin nastavlja isti posao, a još više kad je sin bolji od njega.

Isto vrijedi i za Isusa. Voditelj podsjeća na Isusove riječi: **„Tko u mene bude vjerovao, činit će i djela veća nego što sam ja činio.“** Tumači ih tako da Isus odlazi Ocu, a njegovi učenici ostaju na zemlji i imaju vremena činiti još veća djela. Isus se, zaključuje Grebenar, raduje kad vidi da ljudi u njegovo ime čine velika djela.

magisterium.assessment: Središnja je misao uglavnom usklađena s Pavlovom radošću što se Krist navješćuje, a Isusovo obećanje o „većim djelima” opravdano se može povezati s plodovima navještaja koji po učenicima dopire do mnogih ljudi. Ipak, objašnjenje „himbenoga” navještaja kao navještaja koji nije „iz srca” pojednostavljuje Pavlovu tvrdnju, a uspjeh Pavlove evangelizacije pripisati samo radovanju tuđem navještaju svodi širi biblijski kontekst na jedan čimbenik.
concerns: Pavao konkretno govori o propovijedanju iz zavisti, suparništva i sebične ambicije, pri čemu neki žele povećati njegovu patnju u zatvoru; zato „himbeno” nije samo općenit nedostatak iskrenosti ili srčanosti. Pavao se raduje jer se Krist navješćuje, ali to ei ne čini njihove motive dobrima niti znači da su nevažni u svakom pogledu.

Usporedba s ocem koji se raduje sinu „boljem od njega” može sugerirati da učenici nadmašuju Krista po veličini ili sili. Crkveno tumačenje naglašava da su veća djela Kristova djela koja se ostvaruju po vjernicima, erityisesti evanđeoski navještaj koji vodi druge vjeri, a ne nadmoć učenika nad Gospodinom.
magisterium.enrichment: U Fil 1 Pavao razlikuje dobre motive od sebičnih, ali se raduje stvarnom navještaju Krista i pouzdaje se u pomoć Duha Svetoga; radost zato nije odobravanje zavisti ili neiskrenosti. „Veća djela” iz Iv 14,12 tumače se kao Kristovo djelovanje kroz učenike, osobito širenje vjere po njihovoj riječi i svjedočanstvu, a ne kao djela kojima bi učenici postali veći od Isusa. Taj navještaj pripada životu ljubavi prema bližnjemu i suradnji s Kristovim spasenjskim djelom.

magisterium.assessment_en: The central thought is mainly aligned with Paul's joy that Christ is proclaimed, and Jesus' promise of „greater works” can reasonably be connected with the fruits of proclamation that reaches many people through the disciples. Nevertheless, explaining „insincere” proclamation as proclamation that is not „from the heart” simplifies Paul's assertion, and attributing the success of Paul's evangelization solely to rejoicing in another's proclamation reduces the broader biblical context to a single factor.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Phil 1 Paul distinguishes good motives from selfish ones, but rejoices in the actual proclamation of Christ and trusts in the help of the Holy Spirit; joy is therefore not approval of envy or insincerity. „Greater works” from Jn 14:12 are interpreted as Christ's action through the disciples, especially the spreading of the faith through their word and testimony, rather than as works by which the disciples would become greater than Jesus. That proclamation belongs to a life of love of neighbor and cooperation with Christ's salvific work.
concerns_en: Paul speaks concretely about preaching out of envy, rivalry, and selfish ambition, where some wish to increase his affliction in imprisonment; therefore „insincere” is not merely a general lack of sincerity or heartiness. Paul rejoices because Christ is proclaimed, but that does not make their motives good nor does it mean that they are unimportant in every respect.

The comparison with a father rejoicing in a son „better than him” can suggest that the disciples surpass Christ in greatness or power. Church interpretation emphasizes that the greater works are Christ's works realized through believers, especially the evangelical proclamation leading others to faith, rather than the superiority of the disciples over the Lord.

sections.subtitle_en: The secret of Paul's success: he rejoiced in another's proclamation
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains why Saint Paul was successful in evangelization
sections.content_en:
Interpreting what was read, Vladimir Grebenar first clarifies the expression "in pretense." According to his words, it is a matter of a proclamation that comes "with some self-interest, not like from the heart." For Paul, however, what matters is only that Jesus is proclaimed, and in that he rejoices and will rejoice.

In this the host sees the **answer to the question of why Paul was so successful in evangelization**: he rejoiced that others proclaimed Christ. Then he invites the listeners to imagine Jesus, the crucified Savior, rejoicing when people proclaim him, carry his name throughout the world, do not disown him, bear witness to him, praise him, and glorify him.

### The carpenter father and the son who surpasses him

To make this accessible, Grebenar uses an image from everyday life. Every parent rejoices when his child succeeds in something he taught him. As an example, he mentions an entrepreneur father, a carpenter, who teaches his son the trade. Such a father rejoices when he sees the son continuing the same work, and even more when the son is better than he is.

The same applies to Jesus. The host recalls Jesus' words: **"Whoever believes in me will also do greater works than I have done."** He interprets them to mean that Jesus goes to the Father, and his disciples remain on earth and have time to do even greater works. Jesus, Grebenar concludes, rejoices when he sees people doing great works in his name.

sections.subtitle: Test vjere: radujete li se kad drugi pronose Isusovo ime?
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj postavlja gledateljima pitanje za samoispitivanje vjere
sections.content:
Iz Pavlova stava Vladimir Grebenar izvodi konkretan **„test vjere“** koji svatko može primijeniti na sebe. Pitanje glasi: raduješ li se kad netko drugi pronosi ime Isusovo? Raduješ li se iskreno, u srcu, kad je netko uspješan u evangelizaciji i kad njegov rad donosi plodove? Je li ti drago reći: „Bravo, vidi kako je ovo lijepo“, kad neki muškarac ili žena lijepo svjedoče o Isusu, mole, a ljudi se obraćaju i spašavaju se životi?

„Ako se raduješ, na pravom si putu“, poručuje voditelj. Blaženima naziva sve koji se raduju onome čemu se Bog raduje, a to su, prema njegovim riječima, **obraćenja ljudi**, bez obzira na to gdje se i kako događaju. Posebno ističe da je Pavao rečenicu „tome se radujem i radovat ću se“ zaključio uskličnikom.

### Žalost zbog propadanja kršćanstva

Isti kriterij djeluje i u suprotnom smjeru. Ako se Krist ne navješćuje i kršćanstvo propada, što se, kako Grebenar navodi, „nažalost vidi vlastitim očima u **zapadnoj Europi**“, onda se vjernici trebaju žalostiti, jer je i Isus zbog toga žalostan. Toliki su dali svoj život da bi se kršćanstvo proširilo, a onda je došla jedna generacija i sve to izgubila. „Evo, to se sad događa“, upozorava voditelj.

### Pred križem, s Duhom Svetim

Grebenar naglašava da Božja riječ prodire duboko u srce i daje jasan kriterij za samoprocjenu. Najbolje je, kaže, kad čovjek sam sebe može ocijeniti prema jasnim mjerilima, a da mu nitko ništa ne mora govoriti. Predlaže da vjernik stane pred križ, preispita se i zamoli Duha Svetoga da mu otkrije istinu o njemu samome:

- raduje li se onome čemu se Isus raduje,
- žalosti li se zbog onoga zbog čega je Isus žalostan.

magisterium.assessment: Radovati se kada se Krist naviješta i ljudi se obraćaju u skladu je s kršćanskom radošću i apostolskim poslanjem; kršćanska je radost pritom spojiva i s patnjom i žalosti. Ipak, radost zbog tuđeg uspjeha nije jedini ni dovoljan „test vjere“, a tvrdnju da je Isus žalostan zbog konkretnih društvenih zbivanja valja iznositi s razboritošću, ne kao pojednostavljenu procjenu Njegovih osjećaja.
concerns: „Ako se raduješ, na pravom si putu“ može zvučati kao da je jedan osjećaj dovoljan za procjenu vjere; kršćanska vjernost uključuje i vjeru, ljubav, obraćenje i ustrajnost.

Tvrdnje o propadanju kršćanstva u zapadnoj Europi i o tome kako je Isus zbog toga žalostan široke su prosudbe koje odlomak ne potkrepljuje konkretnim dokazima; žalost zbog slabljenja vjere može biti primjerena, ali treba je povezati s nadom, molitvom i djelovanjem, a ne s beznađem.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao može biti uzor nesebične radosti zbog navještaja Krista, ali kršćanska radost ne znači da se zanemaruju teškoće: ona može postojati zajedno sa žalosti i patnjom. Crkveni nauk povezuje radost s Kristovom smrću i uskrsnućem te djelovanjem Duha Svetoga, pa ona nije samo reakcija na vidljiv uspjeh evangelizacije.

Evangelii Gaudium

magisterium.assessment_en: Rejoicing when Christ is proclaimed and people convert is in accordance with Christian joy and the apostolic mission; Christian joy is at the same time compatible with suffering and sorrow. Nevertheless, joy over another's success is not the only nor a sufficient „test of faith”, and the claim that Jesus is sorrowful over concrete social developments should be put forward with prudence, not as a simplified assessment of His feelings.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul can be a model of unselfish joy over the proclamation of Christ, but Christian joy does not mean that hardships are ignored: it can exist alongside sorrow and suffering. Church teaching connects joy with Christ's Death and Resurrection and the action of the Holy Spirit, so it is not merely a reaction to visible evangelization success.
concerns_en: „If you rejoice, you are on the right path” can sound as though a single feeling is sufficient to assess faith; Christian fidelity also includes faith, charity, conversion, and perseverance.

Claims about the decline of Christianity in Western Europe and about how Jesus is sorrowful because of it are broad judgments that the passage does not substantiate with concrete evidence; sorrow over the weakening of faith can be appropriate, but should be connected with hope, prayer, and action, rather than with despair.

sections.subtitle_en: Test of faith: do you rejoice when others spread Jesus' name?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks the viewers a question for self-examination of faith
sections.content_en:
From Paul's attitude, Vladimir Grebenar derives a concrete **"test of faith"** that anyone can apply to themselves. The question is: do you rejoice when someone else spreads the name of Jesus? Do you rejoice sincerely, in your heart, when someone is successful in evangelization and when their work bears fruit? Are you glad to say: "Well done, look how beautiful this is," when a man or woman bears beautiful witness to Jesus, prays, and people convert and lives are saved?

"If you rejoice, you are on the right track," the host says. He calls blessed all who rejoice in what God rejoices in, which, according to his words, are the **conversions of people**, regardless of where and how they happen. He especially emphasizes that Paul concluded the sentence "in that I rejoice and will rejoice" with an exclamation mark.

### Sorrow over the decline of Christianity

The same criterion works in the opposite direction as well. If Christ is not proclaimed and Christianity is declining, which, as Grebenar states, "is unfortunately seen with one's own eyes in **Western Europe**," then believers should grieve, because Jesus is also sorrowful about it. So many gave their lives so that Christianity would spread, and then a generation came and lost it all. "Look, that is happening right now," the host warns.

### Before the cross, with the Holy Spirit

Grebenar emphasizes that the word of God penetrates deep into the heart and provides a clear criterion for self-assessment. It is best, he says, when a person can evaluate himself according to clear standards without anyone having to tell him anything. He suggests that a believer stand before the cross, examine himself, and ask the Holy Spirit to reveal to him the truth about himself:

- whether he rejoices in what Jesus rejoices in,
- whether he is sorrowful over what makes Jesus sorrowful.

sections.subtitle: „Kao što košuta žudi za izvor-vodom“: čežnja utisnuta u ljudsko srce
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj razmatra psalam o čežnji duše za Bogom
sections.content:
Drugi biblijski tekst dana je psalam koji Vladimir Grebenar čita polako i s naglaskom: „Kao što košuta žudi za izvor-vodom, tako duša moja čezne, Bože, za tobom. Žedna mi je duša Boga, Boga živoga. O, kada ću doći lice Božje gledati?“

Voditelj se posebno zadržava na stihu „duša moja gine kada se spomenem kako koračah u mnoštvu predvodeći ga k domu Božjem“ i ponavlja ga. U njemu vidi sliku duše koja se cijela predaje Bogu i koja je žedna Boga živoga.

Grebenar to naziva „predivnim“ i tumači da je **čežnja za Bogom utisnuta u svakog čovjeka**, jer je čovjek otisak Božje slave i stvoren je na sliku Božju. Zato se, zaključuje, čovjek ne može smiriti dok se ne smiri u Bogu.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje Psalma 42 kao izraza duboke čežnje duše za živim Bogom vjerno odgovara biblijskom tekstu i katoličkom nauku da je čovjek stvoren od Boga i za Boga. Zaključak da čovjek nalazi konačno ispunjenje u Bogu dobro je utemeljen, premda ne treba značiti da su ljudska čežnja ili nemir uvijek svjesni ili da se u ovom životu postiže savršena, neprekinuta smirenost.
magisterium.enrichment: Katekizam uči da je želja za Bogom upisana u ljudsko srce jer je čovjek stvoren od Boga i za Boga, a puninu istine i sreće nalazi u zajedništvu s Njim. Psalam pritom ne prikazuje samo čežnju nego i bol, osjećaj napuštenosti i poziv duši da se nada Bogu; zato kršćanska čežnja može ostati živa i usred kušnje.
