magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation of Psalm 42 as an expression of the soul's deep longing for the living God faithfully corresponds to the biblical text and Catholic teaching that man was created by God and for God. The conclusion that man finds ultimate fulfillment in God is well founded, though it need not mean that human longing or restlessness is always conscious or that perfect, uninterrupted serenity is attained in this life.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catechism teaches that the desire for God is written in the human heart because man is created by God and for God, and finds the fullness of truth and happiness in communion with Him. The Psalm does not depict longing alone, but also pain, a sense of abandonment, and a call to the soul to hope in God; therefore Christian longing can remain alive even in the midst of trial.

sections.subtitle_en: "As the deer pants for streams of water": longing imprinted on the human heart
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host reflects on the psalm about the soul's longing for God
sections.content_en:
The second biblical text of the day is a psalm that Vladimir Grebenar reads slowly and with emphasis: "As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul longs for you, O God. My soul thirsts for God, for the living God. O, when shall I come and behold the face of God?"

The host lingers especially on the verse "these things I remember, as I pour out my soul: how I would go with the throng and lead them in procession to the house of God" and repeats it. In it he sees an image of a soul that surrenders itself entirely to God and thirsts for the living God.

Grebenar calls this "wonderful" and explains that **longing for God is imprinted on every human being**, because human being is an imprint of God's glory and was created in the image of God. That is why, he concludes, man cannot find rest until he finds rest in God.

sections.subtitle: Prispodoba o prvim mjestima i Pavlova poniznost
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj povezuje poslanicu svetog Pavla s evanđeljem o svadbi
sections.content:
Evanđelje dana donosi prizor u kojem Isus jedne subote dolazi na objed u kuću nekog farizejskog prvaka. Promatrajući kako uzvanici biraju prva mjesta, kaže im prispodobu. Tko je pozvan na svadbu, neka ne sjeda na prvo mjesto, jer može doći časniji uzvanik, pa će domaćin reći: „Ustupi mjesto ovome“, i on će postiđen morati sjesti na posljednje mjesto. Neka radije odmah sjedne na posljednje, kako bi mu domaćin rekao: „Prijatelju, pomakni se naviše“, što će mu biti na čast pred svim sustolnicima. Ulomak završava riječima: **„Jer svaki koji se uzvisuje bit će ponižen, a koji se ponizuje bit će uzvišen.“**

Vladimir Grebenar ističe da je to tekst nad kojim treba mnogo razmatrati i meditirati. Zatim postavlja pitanje: koja je veza između prvog čitanja i evanđelja?

Odgovor nalazi u prvoj rečenici poslanice. Pavao se raduje što Krista navješćuju **drugi**, a ne zato što to sam čini. To, prema voditelju, pokazuje da je apostol bio **jako ponizan čovjek**. Ponizan čovjek gleda što je Božji interes i Božja volja. Grebenar poniznost definira kao vršenje volje Božje i poslušnost Božjim zahtjevima, a Pavao je upravo tako činio ono što mu je Bog govorio u molitvi.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje ispravno povezuje Isusovo upozorenje protiv samouzvisivanja s Pavlovom radošću što se Krist naviješta, čak i kada ga naviještaju drugi. Ipak, Pavlovo veselje nije jednostavno dokaz da se ne raduje vlastitom propovijedanju, nego pokazuje da mu je važnije širenje Evanđelja nego osobni položaj ili korist.
concerns: Poniznost se djelomično svodi na vršenje Božje volje i poslušnost; to je važan vid poniznosti, ali biblijski kontekst uključuje i odricanje od samouzvisivanja te usmjerenost na Krista i dobro drugih.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusova prispodoba govori o više od opreznog društvenog ponašanja: ona upozorava da čovjek ne prisvaja čast, nego se prepušta Božjem sudu i daru uzvišenja. Pavao se raduje jer je Krist naviješten i onda kada neki propovijedaju iz neiskrenih pobuda; to ne znači da odobrava njihove motive, nego da Evanđelje stavlja ispred osobnog suparništva.

magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation correctly connects Jesus' warning against self-exaltation with Paul's joy that Christ is proclaimed, even when proclaimed by others. Nevertheless, Paul's rejoicing is not simply proof that he does not rejoice in his own preaching, but shows that the spreading of the Gospel is more important to him than personal status or gain.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' parable speaks of more than cautious social behavior: it warns against man arrogating honor to himself, rather surrendering to God's judgment and the gift of exaltation. Paul rejoices because Christ is proclaimed even when some preach from insincere motives; this does not mean he approves of their motives, but that he puts the Gospel ahead of personal rivalry.
concerns_en: Humility is partially reduced to doing God's will and obedience; this is an important aspect of humility, but the biblical context also includes renouncing self-exaltation and focusing on Christ and the good of others.

sections.subtitle_en: The parable of the places of honor and Paul's humility
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host connects Saint Paul's epistle with the gospel about the wedding feast
sections.content_en:
The gospel of the day brings a scene in which Jesus, on a Sabbath, goes to dine at the house of a prominent Pharisee. Observing how the guests choose the places of honor, he tells them a parable. When someone is invited to a wedding banquet, let him not take the place of honor, for a more distinguished guest may arrive, and the host will say: "Give this person your seat," and in shame he will have to take the lowest place. Rather, let him immediately go and sit in the lowest place, so that his host may say to him: "Friend, move up higher," which will be an honor for him in the presence of all his fellow guests. The passage ends with the words: **"For all those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted."**

Vladimir Grebenar emphasizes that this is a text over which one needs to reflect and meditate a great deal. Then he asks the question: what is the connection between the first reading and the gospel?

He finds the answer in the first sentence of the epistle. Paul rejoices that Christ is proclaimed by **others**, and not because he does it himself. That, according to the host, shows that the apostle was **a very humble man**. A humble man looks at what is God's interest and God's will. Grebenar defines humility as doing the will of God and obedience to God's demands, and Paul did precisely that—doing what God spoke to him in prayer.

sections.subtitle: Put u Makedoniju: vjera bez putnog osiguranja
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj opisuje opasnosti Pavlova putovanja u Makedoniju
sections.content:
Kao primjer Pavlove poslušnosti Vladimir Grebenar navodi njegov odlazak u **Makedoniju**. Kad je Bog apostolu u snu dao da ide onamo, on je otišao bez žaljenja i bez razmišljanja, iako je, kako sam piše, znao da ga čekaju nevolje. Voditelj citira Pavlove riječi: „Sve mogu u onome koji me jača“ i „Kad sam slab, onda sam jak.“

Grebenar slikovito opisuje uvjete tog putovanja. Pavao nije kupio avionsku kartu, nego je polako prelazio tisuće kilometara preko mnogih kraljevstava, polja i putova punih divljih zvijeri. Voditelj otvoreno kaže da to ne piše u Svetom pismu, ali smatra da je apostol zasigurno bio u opasnosti da ga neka zvijer rastrgne, jer se tada nije putovalo kao danas, kada čovjek sjedne u automobil ili zrakoplov.

### Ostaviti sve i krenuti u neizvjesno

„Pokrenuti se i na riječ Božju otići na drugi kraj svijeta, to je vjera“, poručuje Grebenar. Uspoređuje to s današnjim putovanjima, na koja ljudi ne kreću bez putnog osiguranja koje im refundira troškove liječnika ako se tko razboli. Pavao nije imao ni posao ni socijalnu naknadu, a opasnost ga je vrebala na svakom koraku. Voditelj podsjeća da je apostol u jednom tekstu nabrojio koliko je puta bio kamenovan, bičevan i koliko je brodoloma preživio.

Za Pavla je, zaključuje Grebenar, bilo važno samo jedno: vodi li ga riječ Božja. Ako ga vodi, znao je da mu se ništa neće dogoditi. „To je bila vjera i to jest vjera.“

magisterium.assessment: Dobro je istaknuto da je Pavao prihvatio poslanje u Makedoniju usred neizvjesnosti i da je u nevoljama nalazio oslonac u Kristu. Međutim, tvrdnja da je znao kako mu se, ako ga vodi Božja riječ, ništa neće dogoditi nije u skladu s biblijskim prikazom: u Filipima je bio pretučen i zatvoren, a poslije je govorio o progonstvima koja ga čekaju.
concerns: Božje vodstvo ne jamči izbavljenje od tjelesne opasnosti, bolesti ili progona; tumačenje može pogrešno sugerirati takvu zaštitu.
Opis opasnosti od divljih zvijeri izričito je označen kao pretpostavka, a ne kao biblijska tvrdnja; Djela apostolska opisuju plovidbu Pavla i njegovih suputnika prema Makedoniji.
magisterium.enrichment: U Djelima apostolskim Pavao i njegovi suputnici zaključuju da ih Bog poziva naviještati Evanđelje u Makedoniji, ali ondje Pavao i Sila bivaju pretučeni i zatvoreni. To pokazuje da vjera i poslušnost znače pouzdanje u Boga i vjernost poslanju, a ne sigurnost da se vjerniku neće dogoditi zlo. Pavlove riječi o snazi u Kristu treba razumjeti kao pouzdanje da Krist podupire vjernika u slabosti i kušnji, a ne kao obećanje da će ga sačuvati od svake nevolje.

magisterium.assessment_en: It is well highlighted that Paul accepted the mission to Macedonia in the midst of uncertainty and found support in Christ during tribulations. However, the claim that he knew that nothing would happen to him if the word of God guided him is not in accordance with the biblical depiction: in Philippi he was beaten and imprisoned, and later spoke of the persecutions awaiting him.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In the Acts of the Apostles, Paul and his companions conclude that God is calling them to proclaim the Gospel in Macedonia, but there Paul and Silas are beaten and imprisoned. This shows that faith and obedience mean trust in God and fidelity to the mission, not certainty that evil will not happen to the believer. Paul's words about strength in Christ should be understood as trust that Christ supports the believer in weakness and trial, rather than as a promise that he will preserve him from all tribulation.
concerns_en: God's guidance does not guarantee deliverance from physical danger, illness, or persecution; the interpretation can mistakenly suggest such protection.
The description of danger from wild beasts is explicitly marked as a supposition rather than a biblical statement; the Acts of the Apostles describe Paul and his companions sailing toward Macedonia.

sections.subtitle_en: Journey to Macedonia: faith without travel insurance
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host describes the dangers of Paul's journey to Macedonia
sections.content_en:
As an example of Paul's obedience, Vladimir Grebenar cites his departure for **Macedonia**. When God gave the apostle in a dream to go there, he went without regret and without second thoughts, even though, as he himself writes, he knew that hardships awaited him. The host quotes Paul's words: "I can do all things through him who strengthens me" and "When I am weak, then I am strong."

Grebenar vividly describes the conditions of that journey. Paul did not buy a plane ticket, but slowly crossed thousands of kilometers across many kingdoms, fields, and paths full of wild beasts. The host openly says that this is not written in Holy Scripture, but believes that the apostle was certainly in danger of being torn apart by some beast, because back then people did not travel as they do today, when a person sits in a car or an airplane.

### Leaving everything and heading into the unknown

"To get moving and go to the other side of the world at the word of God, that is faith," Grebenar conveys. He compares this with today's travels, on which people do not set out without travel insurance that reimburses doctor expenses if someone falls ill. Paul had neither a job nor social assistance, and danger lurked for him at every step. The host recalls that the apostle in one text listed how many times he had been stoned, beaten, and how many shipwrecks he had survived.

For Paul, Grebenar concludes, only one thing mattered: whether the word of God was guiding him. If it was guiding him, he knew that nothing would happen to him. "That was faith, and that is faith."

sections.subtitle: Sjesti na posljednje mjesto: Bog izabire one koji to ne žele
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o tome da Bog za velika djela izabire one koji ih ne žele
sections.content:
Vraćajući se evanđelju, Vladimir Grebenar tumači da će oni koji sebe vide na nekoj poziciji biti poniženi. Ljudi koji sjedaju na prva mjesta, kaže, **ne vide što je Božji interes** i ne raduju se onome čemu se Bog raduje. Da bi se netko mogao radovati onome čemu se Bog raduje, mora sjesti na posljednje mjesto.

Želja srca, prema voditelju, mora biti da se čovjek ponizi i pred Bogom i pred ljudima te da ne želi biti „nešto veliko u životu“. Razlog je jednostavan: **„Bog izabire za velika djela one koji to ne žele.“**

### Kad poziv dođe tamo gdje ga ne želiš

Grebenar objašnjava da Bog često pozove čovjeka upravo na djelo koje taj čovjek ne želi, jer mu je potrebna njegova ili njezina poniznost. Čovjek pristaje samo zato što to Bog traži. Najčešće ni ne zna kako će to izvesti, pa se mora osloniti na milost i pitati: „Kako će to biti? Ja ne znam kako će to biti.“ Tada ga, kaže voditelj, vodi milost Božja, Bog izvanredno upotrijebi njegove talente i sve se poklopi.

Isus time poučava da **pozicija i hijerarhija pripadaju onima koji ih ne žele**. Grebenar to sažima kao poziv da čovjek traži najnižu razinu privilegija i ondje sjedi, pa će ga Bog podići ako to bude htio.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na poniznost i služenje u skladu je s Isusovom poukom da se onaj koji se uzvisuje ponizuje, a ponizni uzvisuje, te da među učenicima veličina znači služenje, a ne traženje časti. Ipak, tvrdnje da Bog izabire upravo one koji ne žele velika djela i da položaji pripadaju onima koji ih ne žele previše su općenite: poniznost nije prezir prema vlastitim darovima ni pravilo da će Bog nužno dodijeliti položaj onome tko ga ne želi.
concerns: Formulacija o Božjem izboru može pogrešno sugerirati da je nevoljkost ili opiranje samo po sebi znak poziva od Boga.
„Sjediti na posljednjem mjestu” može zvučati kao taktika kojom se zaslužuje unapređenje; evanđeoska poniznost traži služenje bez proračuna o budućoj časti.
magisterium.enrichment: U Lk 14, 7–11 Isusov savjet o posljednjem mjestu razotkriva samouzvisivanje i usmjerava učenika na poniznost, a ne na zajamčenu društvenu ili crkvenu promociju. Kršćansko vodstvo ne ukida službe i odgovornosti, nego ih preobražava u služenje po uzoru na Krista, koji je došao služiti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to humility and service is in accordance with Jesus' teaching that whoever exalts himself will be humbled and the humble will be exalted, and that among the disciples greatness means service rather than seeking honors. Nevertheless, the claims that God chooses precisely those who do not want great deeds and that positions belong to those who do not want them are overly generalized: humility is neither contempt for one's gifts nor a rule that God will necessarily grant a position to whoever does not want it.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Lk 14:7–11 Jesus' advice about the last place exposes self-exaltation and directs the disciple toward humility, rather than toward guaranteed social or ecclesial promotion. Christian leadership does not abolish offices and responsibilities, but transforms them into service after the model of Christ, who came to serve.
concerns_en: The formulation concerning God's choice can mistakenly suggest that reluctance or resistance in itself is a sign of a call from God.
„Sitting in the last place” can sound like a tactic by which advancement is merited; evangelical humility demands service without calculating future honor.

sections.subtitle_en: Sitting in the lowest place: God chooses those who do not want it
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about how God chooses those who do not want them for great works
sections.content_en:
Returning to the gospel, Vladimir Grebenar interprets that those who see themselves in some position will be humbled. People who sit in the places of honor, he says, **do not see what God's interest is** and do not rejoice in what God rejoices in. In order for someone to be able to rejoice in what God rejoices in, he must sit in the lowest place.

The desire of the heart, according to the host, must be for a person to humble himself both before God and before people, and not to want to be "something big in life." The reason is simple: **"God chooses for great works those who do not want them."**

### When the call comes where you do not want it

Grebenar explains that God often calls a person precisely to a work that that person does not want, because he needs his or her humility. A person consents solely because God asks it. Most often he does not even know how he will carry it out, so he must rely on grace and ask: "How will this be? I do not know how this will be." Then, the host says, God's grace leads him, God extraordinarily employs his talents, and everything falls into place.

Jesus thereby teaches that **position and hierarchy belong to those who do not want them**. Grebenar summarizes this as a call for a person to seek the lowest level of privileges and sit there, and then God will raise him up if he wants to.

sections.subtitle: Osobno svjedočanstvo: „Mislio sam da je to moj kraj“
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar svjedoči o strahu kada je pozvan pokrenuti podcast
sections.content:
Ovu pouku Vladimir Grebenar potkrepljuje vlastitim iskustvom. Kada molitvenu inicijativu i zajednicu Ora et Labora naziva najvećom molitvenom zajednicom na svijetu, kaže da to ne govori zbog sebe, jer to nije njegovo djelo, nego **Gospodinovo**.

Kad ga je Gospodin pozvao da preko interneta pokrene molitvu i tumačenje Božje riječi, priznaje da je pomislio kako je to njegov kraj. Imao je dobar posao i visoko obrazovanje, a bojao se da će si uništiti posao i sve ostalo.

### Strah za poslovni ugled

Grebenar opisuje prirodu svoga posla. Direktori i vlasnici poduzeća zovu ga da rješava teške probleme u poslovnim organizacijama i uvodi nove modele organizacije, što zahtijeva veliko međusobno povjerenje. U tvrtkama sa 100, 200 ili 300 zaposlenih predaje menadžerima, kojih je ponekad 30, a ponekad i 50. Znao je da će oni čim se pojavi upisati njegovo ime i prezime u internetsku tražilicu. Bojao se da će, vide li da snima vjerske podcaste koje prati 50 ljudi, nekolicina reći direktoru: „Koga si ovo doveo? Ovo je neki vjerski fanatik.“

To naziva svojom palom ljudskom naravi. Dodaje da mu je i neprijatelj šaputao: „Odustani, ne idi u to, uništit ćeš se.“ Slično su govorili i neki ljudi koji ga poznaju, „pod navodnicima dobronamjerni“, upozoravajući ga da će uništiti i sebe i obitelj.

### „Ne želim, ali ako je tvoja volja…“

Unatoč svemu, Grebenar je u srcu čuo poziv. Priznaje da je osjećao **ogroman otpor** prema molitvi preko interneta. Poziv je uključivao i preseljenje u **Međugorje**. Bogu je odgovorio: „Ja to ništa ne želim, ali ako je to tvoja volja, ja ću to učiniti.“

Danas ističe plodove i broj ljudi koji su se obratili, „ne zbog mene, nego samo zato što sam poslušao“. Bogu je, poručuje, dovoljno da čovjek posluša.

Rizik je bio stvaran. Kao poduzetnik ima, kako kaže, vrlo riskantan posao. Poduzetnici se međusobno raspituju o suradnicima, pa su dovoljna dva ili tri neuspjela projekta da čovjek dobije etiketu nakon koje ga nitko više ne zove. Uz to su obitelj i djeca. Snimati još i vjerski podcast za njegov je razum bilo „totalno udaranje glavom u zid“.

magisterium.assessment: Osobno svjedočanstvo o odricanju od vlastite sigurnosti radi mogućeg Božjeg poziva u osnovi je spojivo s kršćanskom poslušnošću i povjerenjem u milost. Ipak, iz opisa nije moguće potvrditi da je konkretan unutarnji poticaj sigurno bio Božji poziv, a rečenica da je Bogu dovoljno da čovjek posluša ne bi smjela značiti da svaki snažan dojam treba slijediti bez razlučivanja.
concerns: Unutarnji otpor ili strah sam po sebi ne dokazuje da Bog poziva baš na ono što osoba ne želi.
Tvrdnja o plodovima i obraćenjima prenesena je kao osobno svjedočanstvo; dostupni sadržaj ne omogućuje neovisnu teološku ili činjeničnu procjenu tih plodova.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko shvaćanje poslušnosti nije slijepo prepuštanje svakom unutarnjem poticaju: Božja riječ treba biti temelj i mjerilo izbora, a razlučivanje uključuje promišljanje i provjeru poziva. Kada se poziv razazna, poslušnost može uključivati stvarnu žrtvu i oslanjanje na Boga, ali se ne smije poistovjetiti s obećanjem uspjeha, ugleda ili određenih vidljivih rezultata.

magisterium.assessment_en: Personal testimony about renouncing one's own security for the sake of a possible call from God is fundamentally compatible with Christian obedience and trust in grace. Nevertheless, from the description it is not possible to confirm that a concrete internal impulse was definitely God's call, and the sentence that it is enough for God that man obeys should not mean that every strong impression should be followed without discernment.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of obedience is not blind surrender to every internal impulse: God's word should be the foundation and standard of choice, and discernment includes reflection and testing the call. When a call is discerned, obedience can involve real sacrifice and reliance on God, but must not be equated with a promise of success, reputation, or specific visible results.
concerns_en: Internal resistance or fear does not in itself prove that God is calling precisely to what the person does not want.
The claim about fruits and conversions is conveyed as personal testimony; the available content does not allow for an independent theological or factual assessment of those fruits.

sections.subtitle_en: Personal testimony: "I thought it was the end of me"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar testifies about fear when he was called to start a podcast
sections.content_en:
Vladimir Grebenar corroborates this lesson with his own experience. When he calls the prayer initiative and community Ora et Labora the largest prayer community in the world, he says he does not say this because of himself, because it is not his work, but **the Lord's**.

When the Lord called him to launch prayer and the interpretation of the word of God over the internet, he admits he thought that was the end of him. He had a good job and a higher education, and he was afraid he would ruin his business and everything else.

### Fear for business reputation

Grebenar describes the nature of his work. Company directors and owners call him to solve difficult problems in business organizations and introduce new organizational models, which requires great mutual trust. In companies with 100, 200, or 300 employees, he lectures to managers, of whom there are sometimes 30, and sometimes 50. He knew that as soon as he appeared, they would type his first and last name into an internet search engine. He was afraid that, if they saw he recorded religious podcasts followed by 50 people, a few would tell the director: "Who did you bring in here? This is some religious fanatic."

He calls this his fallen human nature. He adds that the enemy also whispered to him: "Give up, don't go into that, you will destroy yourself." Some people who know him, "well-meaning in quotation marks," spoke similarly, warning him that he would destroy both himself and his family.

### "I don't want to, but if it is your will…"

Despite everything, Grebenar heard a call in his heart. He admits he felt **enormous resistance** toward prayer over the internet. The call also included moving to **Međugorje**. He answered God: "I don't want any of this, but if it is your will, I will do it."

Today he highlights the fruits and the number of people who converted, "not because of me, but only because I obeyed." For God, he conveys, it is enough for a person to obey.

The risk was real. As an entrepreneur, he has, as he says, a very risky job. Entrepreneurs ask each other about associates, so two or three failed projects are enough for a person to get a label after which no one calls him anymore. Along with that are family and children. To record a religious podcast on top of that was, for his reason, "totally banging one's head against a wall."

sections.subtitle: Srce ispred razuma i plodovi koje ljudi vide u svojim životima
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj opisuje kako ljudi na skupu u Prozoru dižu ruke svjedočeći o promjeni života
sections.content:
Iz svog iskustva Vladimir Grebenar izvodi duhovno načelo: Bog upravo tako postupa s čovjekom. Dopušta mu da u duhovnom smislu „racijom opali glavom o duhovni zid“, kako bi shvatio da razum pred Bogom ne vrijedi ništa. **Srce je puno važnije.**

To, međutim, ne znači odbacivanje razuma. Kada je srce na Božjoj strani, objašnjava voditelj, Bog oblikuje i razum. Čovjek tada razumije puno dublje i šire i otvaraju mu se nove dimenzije, jer riječ Gospodnju prima srcem.

### Svjedočanstva s terena

U tome Grebenar vidi i razlog zašto ga toliki ljudi slušaju na skupovima. Opisuje kako na susretima, poput onoga koji ga čeka toga dana u **Prozoru**, pita prisutne koliko ih prati emisiju. Ruku podigne otprilike dvije trećine. Na pitanje koliko ih je raslo u vjeri i kome se promijenio život, ponovno se dižu ruke.

Čovjeka se u tome ne može prevariti, naglašava voditelj. Svatko zna je li mu se život promijenio i je li mu nešto bilo na izgradnju ili na štetu. Nitko izvana ne može uvjeriti čovjeka da mu se život nije promijenio, a za tako bitne stvari ljudima, kaže, ne trebaju ni odvjetnici ni tumači.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak da vjera zahvaća srce, preobražava osobu i može produbiti njezino razumijevanje uglavnom je katolički, ali tvrdnja da razum pred Bogom ne vrijedi ništa preoštra je ako se shvati doslovno. Također, osobno svjedočanstvo o promjeni života može biti važno, ali samo po sebi ne dokazuje istinitost svakog tumačenja ili učenja.
concerns: Izraz da razum pred Bogom ne vrijedi ništa može stvoriti dojam da je razum nevažan ili suprotan vjeri; katoličko shvaćanje vjere uključuje i razum i volju, dok je srce biblijski shvaćeno kao središte cijele osobe, a ne kao zamjena za razum.

Tvrdnja da čovjek sam zna je li mu se život promijenio govori o osobnom iskustvu, ali taj doživljaj nije samostalan mjerodavan kriterij za prosudbu istinitosti vjerskog nauka. Kršćanska vjera prima se osobno, ali je ujedno crkvena i odgovara na sadržaj Evanđelja.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao govori da se vjeruje srcem, a crkveno tumačenje ovdje srce razumije kao mjesto susreta intelekta, volje, osjećaja i otvorenosti istini i ljubavi; zato je primjerenije reći da vjera pročišćuje i prosvjetljuje razum nego da ga obezvređuje. Plodovi promijenjenog života mogu biti znak djelovanja Evanđelja, ali ih valja promatrati zajedno s vjernošću Kristu i sadržaju vjere, a ne kao zamjenu za njih.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that faith touches the heart, transforms the person, and can deepen their understanding is mainly Catholic, but the claim that reason is worth nothing before God is too sharp if taken literally. Also, personal testimony about a changed life can be important, but in itself does not prove the truth of every interpretation or teaching.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul speaks of believing with the heart, and Church interpretation here understands the heart as the meeting place of intellect, will, feelings, and openness to truth and love; therefore it is more appropriate to say that faith purifies and enlightens reason than that it devalues it. The fruits of a changed life can be a sign of the Gospel's work, but they should be viewed together with fidelity to Christ and the content of faith, rather than as a substitute for them.
concerns_en: The expression that reason is worth nothing before God can create the impression that reason is unimportant or contrary to faith; the Catholic understanding of faith includes both reason and will, while the heart is biblically understood as the center of the entire person, not as a replacement for reason.

The claim that a person knows for himself whether his life has changed speaks of personal experience, but that experience is not an independent authoritative criterion for judging the truth of religious doctrine. Christian faith is received personally, but is at the same time ecclesial and responds to the content of the Gospel.

sections.subtitle_en: Heart before reason and the fruits that people see in their lives
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host describes how people at the gathering in Prozor raise their hands testifying to a life change
sections.content_en:
From his experience, Vladimir Grebenar derives a spiritual principle: God treats man in precisely that way. He allows him in a spiritual sense to "smash his head against a spiritual wall with reason," in order to realize that reason is worth nothing before God. **The heart is much more important.**

This, however, does not mean discarding reason. When the heart is on God's side, the host explains, God also shapes reason. A person then understands much more deeply and broadly, and new dimensions open up to him, because he receives the word of the Lord with his heart.

### Testimonies from the field

In this, Grebenar also sees the reason why so many people listen to him at gatherings. He describes how at meetings, like the one awaiting him that day in **Prozor**, he asks attendees how many of them follow the broadcast. Approximately two-thirds raise their hands. At the question of how many grew in faith and whose life was changed, hands are raised again.

A person cannot be deceived in this, the host emphasizes. Everyone knows whether their life changed and whether something was for their edification or detriment. No one from outside can convince a person that their life did not change, and for such essential things people, he says, need neither lawyers nor interpreters.

sections.subtitle: Zamka priznanja: „Nikad nisam htio voditi molitvenu zajednicu“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o tome kako nikada nije težio vodstvu ni priznanju
sections.content:
Vladimir Grebenar zatim formulira jedno od ključnih načela tumačenja: tko želi biti uspješan u evangelizaciji, ali i u životu, mora **odbaciti želju da bude netko i nešto i da ga ljudi priznaju**. „To je opasno. To je zamka“, upozorava.

Potom ponovno govori o sebi. Godinama, kaže, nije imao takvih želja i nikada nije htio voditi molitvenu zajednicu. Dok je sudjelovao u **duhovnim vježbama svetog Ignacija**, nije ga zanimalo nikakvo vodstvo. Pratio je samo svoju djecu, kojih je, kako kaže, bilo dosta, i to mu je bilo puno. Važno mu je bilo dovesti djecu da čuju Božju riječ. Koliko je u tome uspio, „vrijeme će pokazati“, iako vjeruje da je uz Božju milost u mnogočemu uspio.

Nikada nije želio biti voditelj molitvene zajednice ili inicijative, a ni direktor u poduzeću ili netko u hijerarhiji. Takav stav naziva važnim preduvjetom da Bog čovjeka može izabrati za neko djelo i zahvalan je Bogu na njemu. Svoje svjedočanstvo zaključuje ponavljanjem misli da **hijerarhija pripada onima koji je ne traže**, a vrše volju Božju i raduju se onome čemu se Bog raduje.

magisterium.assessment: Upozorenje protiv taštine, želje za priznanjem i traženja položaja radi vlastite važnosti dobro odgovara Isusovu učenju o poniznosti i služenju. Ipak, tvrdnja da hijerarhija pripada onima koji je ne traže te da je takav stav preduvjet Božjeg izbora može zvučati kao opće pravilo koje zanemaruje poziv, razlučivanje i odgovorno prihvaćanje službe.
concerns: Odbacivanje ambicije i taštine ne treba poistovjetiti s tvrdnjom da svatko tko prihvati voditeljsku službu nužno postupa neponizno; crkvena služba može biti odgovor na Božji poziv, a njezin kriterij je služenje, ne dominacija ili osobna korist.

Formulacija da hijerarhija pripada onima koji je ne traže izrečena je preširoko: ne tražiti položaj može biti znak slobode od taštine, ali samo po sebi ne potvrđuje da je netko pozvan ili prikladan za određenu službu.
magisterium.enrichment: Isus ne osuđuje svaku želju za velikodušnim služenjem ili odgovornošću, nego ambiciju koja traži prvenstvo i vlast radi sebe: tko želi biti velik, pozvan je postati sluga svima. Zato je naglasak na nezainteresiranosti za osobni prestiž zdrav, dok vodstvo valja razumjeti kao službu koju se prihvaća u poslušnosti pozivu i usmjerava prema dobru zajednice.

magisterium.assessment_en: The warning against vanity, the desire for recognition, and seeking positions for the sake of one's own importance corresponds well to Jesus' teaching on humility and service. Nevertheless, the claim that hierarchy belongs to those who do not seek it and that such an attitude is a precondition for God's choice can sound like a general rule that ignores vocation, discernment, and the responsible acceptance of ministry.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus does not condemn every desire for generous service or responsibility, but ambition that seeks primacy and power for oneself: whoever wishes to be great is called to become the servant of all. Therefore, the emphasis on disinterest in personal prestige is sound, while leadership should be understood as a service accepted in obedience to a call and directed toward the good of the community.
concerns_en: Rejecting ambition and vanity should not be equated with the claim that anyone who accepts a leadership ministry necessarily acts without humility; ecclesial ministry can be a response to God's call, and its criterion is service, not domination or personal gain.

The formulation that hierarchy belongs to those who do not seek it is stated too broadly: not seeking a position can be a sign of freedom from vanity, but in itself does not confirm that someone is called or suitable for a particular ministry.

sections.subtitle_en: The trap of recognition: "I never wanted to lead a prayer community"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about how he never strived for leadership or recognition
sections.content_en:
Vladimir Grebenar then formulates one of the key principles of the interpretation: whoever wants to be successful in evangelization, but also in life, must **reject the desire to be somebody and something and to be recognized by people**. "That is dangerous. That is a trap," he warns.

Then he speaks about himself again. For years, he says, he had no such desires and never wanted to lead a prayer community. While participating in the **Spiritual Exercises of Saint Ignatius**, he was not interested in any leadership. He was only following his children, of whom, as he says, there were quite a few, and that was plenty for him. What mattered to him was bringing the children to hear the word of God. How much he succeeded in that, "time will tell," although he believes that with God's grace he succeeded in many things.

He never wanted to be a leader of a prayer community or initiative, nor a director in an enterprise, or someone in the hierarchy. He calls such an attitude an important prerequisite for God to be able to choose a person for a work, and he is grateful to God for it. He concludes his testimony by repeating the thought that **hierarchy belongs to those who do not seek it**, but do the will of God and rejoice in what God rejoices in.

sections.subtitle: Tko strpljivo čeka s Gospodinom, dočeka svoju priliku
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj izriče pravilo o strpljivom čekanju s Gospodinom
sections.content:
Vladimir Grebenar upozorava i na drugu stranu evanđeoske pouke. One koji teže vlastitoj slavi i guraju se ondje gdje im nije mjesto **Bog će poniziti**, srušit će ih s tog trona „i bit će to bolno“. Zato Isus savjetuje da se traže zadnja mjesta. Tada će onaj koji dijeli pozicije, a to je Bog, čovjeka staviti na pravo mjesto i reći mu: „Prijatelju, pomakni se naviše.“

Voditelj dodaje i vlastito zapažanje. Kad vidi ljude kojima je važno biti netko u organizaciji i koji se guraju, smatra to znakom da to mjesto nije za njih. Isto vrijedi za one koji ne mogu neko vrijeme istrpjeti razinu nižu od svojih sposobnosti.

### Čišćenje na nižoj razini odgovornosti

Bog, objašnjava Grebenar, može nekoga godinu, dvije, tri ili pet godina držati na razini odgovornosti nižoj od njegovih sposobnosti. Razlog je to što takav čovjek možda jest intelektualno spreman, ali **duhovno nije**. Ako ga Bog priprema za veliko djelo, može ga staviti na nižu razinu kako bi ga očistio i pripremio, a onda ga u pravom trenutku podići puno više nego što je ikad mislio.

Odatle proizlazi pravilo koje voditelj, kako kaže, poznaje iz iskustva: **tko strpljivo čeka s Gospodinom, dočeka svoju priliku.** Bog je savršeno pravedan i svatko će dobiti svoju priliku. Nije moguće, tvrdi Grebenar, da Bog poniznog i poslušnog čovjeka koji vrši njegovu volju ne postavi u pravi trenutak na pravo mjesto, a taj trenutak određuje Bog. Zato nema žurbe. Jedina dopuštena žurba je biti brz i spreman činiti ono što čovjeku dolazi u molitvi.

Ljudske mudrolije i planovi, prema voditelju, ne vrijede ništa. Podsjeća na psalam: **„Ako Jahve kuću ne gradi, uzalud se trude graditelji.“** Tko gradi neko djelo, neka ga gradi s Gospodinom, prihvati mjesto na kojem se sada nalazi i strpljivo čeka govoreći: „Bože, evo me, ako treba i do kraja života ovdje biti.“

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na poniznost, strpljivost, molitvu i povjerenje u Božju providnost uglavnom je u skladu s Isusovom poukom da će onaj tko se uzvisuje biti ponižen, a ponizni uzvišen, te s Psalmom 127 o ovisnosti ljudskog rada o Bogu. Ipak, tvrdnja da će svaki ponizan i poslušan čovjek sigurno dobiti priliku i biti postavljen na odgovarajuće mjesto može zvučati kao obećanje zemaljskog napredovanja koje evanđelje ne jamči.
concerns: Poniznost ne treba tumačiti kao strategiju kojom se zaslužuje viši položaj: Isusova pouka prvenstveno osuđuje samouzvisivanje i poziva na poniznost, a ne obećava napredovanje u organizaciji ili uspjeh prema vlastitim sposobnostima.
Izraz „svatko će dobiti svoju priliku” previše je kategoričan ako znači da će Bog svakome u ovom životu osigurati željenu ulogu ili priznanje; Božja providnost nije jamstvo zemaljskog uspjeha.

Pretpostavka da je guranje za odgovorno mjesto znak da ono nije za tu osobu može biti korisno upozorenje protiv ambicije, ali sama po sebi nije pouzdan kriterij za razlučivanje poziva ili sposobnosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusova pouka o posljednjem mjestu u Lk 14,11 usmjerena je na poniznost pred Bogom, a ne na taktiku koja će nužno donijeti viši rang. Psalm 127 potvrđuje da ljudski trud treba Božju pomoć, ali ne poništava odgovorno planiranje i rad: Benedikt XVI. ističe i potrebu zauzimanja svih članova zajednice i primat Božje potpore. Zato se strpljivost može razumjeti kao vjernost u sadašnjem poslanju, čak i kada željena prilika ne dođe ili poprimi drukčiji oblik.

citations.document_title: Acta Apostolicae Sedis: Issue 9, September, 2007
General Audience of 31 August 2005: Psalm 127[126] - If the Lord does not build the house

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to humility, patience, prayer, and trust in God's providence is mainly in accordance with Jesus' instruction that whoever exalts himself will be humbled and the humble exalted, and with Psalm 127 on the dependence of human labor on God. Nevertheless, the claim that every humble and obedient person will surely get an opportunity and be placed in the appropriate place can sound like a promise of earthly advancement that the Gospel does not guarantee.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' instruction on the last place in Lk 14:11 is directed toward humility before God, rather than toward a tactic that will necessarily bring higher rank. Psalm 127 confirms that human toil needs God's help, but does not negate responsible planning and labor: Benedict XVI highlights both the need for the engagement of all members of the community and the primacy of God's support. Therefore, patience can be understood as fidelity in one's present mission, even when the desired opportunity does not come or takes a different form.
concerns_en: Humility should not be interpreted as a strategy by which a higher position is merited: Jesus' instruction primarily condemns self-exaltation and calls to humility, rather than promising advancement in an organization or success according to one's abilities.

The expression „everyone will get their chance” is too categorical if it means that God will secure for everyone in this life a desired role or recognition; God's providence is not a guarantee of earthly success.

The assumption that pushing for a responsible position is a sign that it is not for that person can be a useful warning against ambition, but in itself is not a reliable criterion for discerning a call or abilities.

sections.subtitle_en: Whoever waits patiently with the Lord will meet his opportunity
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host utters the rule about waiting patiently with the Lord
sections.content_en:
Vladimir Grebenar also warns of the other side of the gospel lesson. Those who strive for their own glory and push themselves where they do not belong **God will humble**, he will cast them down from that throne "and it will be painful." That is why Jesus advises seeking the lowest places. Then the one who distributes positions, who is God, will place the person in the right place and say to him: "Friend, move up higher."

The host also adds his own observation. When he sees people for whom it is important to be someone in an organization and who push themselves, he considers that a sign that the place is not for them. The same applies to those who cannot endure for some time a level lower than their abilities.

### Cleansing at a lower level of responsibility

God, Grebenar explains, can keep someone for a year, two, three, or five years at a level of responsibility lower than his abilities. The reason is that such a person may be intellectually ready, but **spiritually he is not**. If God is preparing him for a great work, he can place him at a lower level to cleanse and prepare him, and then at the right moment raise him up much higher than he ever thought.

From this arises the rule that the host, as he says, knows from experience: **whoever waits patiently with the Lord will meet his opportunity.** God is perfectly just and everyone will get their opportunity. It is not possible, Grebenar claims, that God would not place a humble and obedient person who does his will in the right place at the right moment, and that moment is determined by God. Therefore, there is no rush. The only permitted hurry is to be prompt and ready to do what comes to a person in prayer.

Human cleverness and plans, according to the host, are worth nothing. He recalls the psalm: **"Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain."** Whoever builds a work, let him build it with the Lord, accept the place where he currently is, and wait patiently, saying: "God, here I am, even if I have to stay here until the end of my life."

sections.subtitle: Rezultati kao štit: od sporta do evangelizacije
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj uspoređuje važnost rezultata kod nogometnog trenera i u evangelizaciji
sections.content:
Zatvarajući krug, Vladimir Grebenar se vraća svetom Pavlu. Apostol se radovao što drugi navješćuju Krista i zato ga je, prema voditeljevu tumačenju, Bog podigao da je mogao „cijelu Europu pokrstiti“. Pavao je znao koja je temeljna vrijednost njegova života: Isus, koji je za njega dobitak, „kako je lijepo napisao“.

Na tom tragu Grebenar poziva slušatelje da preispitaju svoj život. Vjernici bi se, kaže, trebali baviti pitanjem **što oni sami čine za Isusa**, a ne što čine drugi. Kad čuju za tuđi trud, neka se raduju, a zatim neka se zapitaju: „Vidi drugoga kako čini. A što ja činim? Gdje su moji rezultati?“

### „Rezultat je najbolji prijatelj“

Voditelj za sebe kaže da je čovjek koji traži rezultate. Rezultat je, prema njegovim riječima, često najbolji, a ponekad i jedini prijatelj. Kad krenu napadi, „bujice“ i protivljenje, rezultati štite i brane, jer protiv njih nitko ne može. To vrijedi u poslu i u sportu. Navijači i uprava kluba mogu ne voljeti nekog trenera, ali ako on ima rezultate, nitko ga ne dira. Isto je u politici i u drugim područjima.

Tako je, zaključuje Grebenar, i u evangelizaciji. Tko ima rezultate, toga štiti milost Božja, jer surađuje s njom. Tumačenje završava pozivom da se vjernici ponize, „pa da nas Bog uzvisi kako on želi“.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv da se vjernici raduju naviještanju Krista, umjesto da zavide drugima, i da vlastiti život usmjere prema Isusu dobro je usklađen s Pavlovim primjerom. No odlomak tu poruku slabi tvrdnjom da rezultati štite navjestitelja i da je Pavao mogao „cijelu Europu pokrstiti”, što može zamijeniti evanđeosku vjernost mjerilom uspjeha i pretjerati u opisu Pavlova djelovanja.
concerns: „Rezultat je najbolji prijatelj” i tvrdnja da protiv rezultata nitko ne može prenose poslovnu ili političku logiku u evangelizaciju; brojčani ili vidljivi uspjeh nije dokaz Božje naklonosti niti zaštita od protivljenja.

Tvrdnja da je Bog podigao Pavla kako bi „cijelu Europu pokrstio” preuveličava ono što odlomak može opravdati: izneseni izvori podupiru Pavlovu radost što se naviješta Krist, ne tvrdnju da je Pavao pokrstio cijelu Europu.
Izraz „štiti milost Božja, jer surađuje s njom” treba pojasniti kako ne bi sugerirao da uspjeh evangelizacije osigurava zaštitu od nevolja ili da se milost može mjeriti rezultatima.
magisterium.enrichment: U Fil 1,18 Pavao se raduje što se Krist naviješta čak i kada su motivi nekih propovjednika neispravni; središte radosti jest Kristovo naviještanje, a ne osobni prestiž ili zaštita od kritike. Katoličko razumijevanje milosti čuva redoslijed: Božji dar i pomirenje prethode ljudskom djelovanju, a apostolsko služenje postaje sredstvo Božjeg djela, ne jamstvo vidljivog uspjeha. Stoga su plodovi evangelizacije razlog za zahvalnost i razlučivanje, ali mjerilo vjernosti ostaje služenje Kristu u ljubavi, uključujući i onda kada su plodovi skromni ili nisu odmah vidljivi.

citations.document_title: Homilies on Philippians
“What is Man?” (Ps 8:5). An itinerary of biblical anthropology

magisterium.assessment_en: The call for believers to rejoice in the proclamation of Christ, instead of envying others, and to direct their own lives toward Jesus is well aligned with Paul's example. But the passage weakens that message with the claim that results protect the proclaimer and that Paul was able to „baptize all of Europe”, which can replace evangelical fidelity with a standard of success and exaggerate in describing Paul's activity.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Phil 1:18 Paul rejoices that Christ is proclaimed even when the motives of some preachers are improper; the center of joy is the proclamation of Christ, not personal prestige or protection from criticism. The Catholic understanding of grace preserves order: God's gift and reconciliation precede human action, and apostolic ministry becomes an instrument of God's work, not a guarantee of visible success. Therefore, the fruits of evangelization are a reason for thanksgiving and discernment, but the standard of fidelity remains serving Christ in love, including when the fruits are modest or not immediately visible.
concerns_en: „The result is the best friend” and the claim that no one can stand against results transfer business or political logic into evangelization; numerical or visible success is not proof of God's favor nor protection against opposition.

The claim that God raised Paul up to „baptize all of Europe” exaggerates what the passage can justify: the presented sources support Paul's joy that Christ is proclaimed, not the claim that Paul baptized all of Europe.

The expression „God's grace protects, because he cooperates with it” should be clarified so as not to suggest that evangelization success secures protection from adversity or that grace can be measured by results.

sections.subtitle_en: Results as a shield: from sports to evangelization
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host compares the importance of results for a football coach and in evangelization
sections.content_en:
Closing the circle, Vladimir Grebenar returns to Saint Paul. The apostle rejoiced that others proclaimed Christ, and that is why, according to the host's interpretation, God raised him up so that he was able to "baptize the whole of Europe." Paul knew the fundamental value of his life: Jesus, who for him was gain, "as he beautifully wrote."

Along those lines, Grebenar invites the listeners to examine their own lives. Believers, he says, should occupy themselves with the question of **what they themselves are doing for Jesus**, and not what others are doing. When they hear of another's effort, let them rejoice, and then let them ask themselves: "Look at the other person doing it. But what am I doing? Where are my results?"

### "Result is the best friend"

The host says of himself that he is a man who seeks results. The result, according to his words, is often the best, and sometimes the only friend. When attacks, "torrents," and opposition begin, results protect and defend, because no one can go against them. This applies in business and in sports. Fans and club management may dislike a coach, but if he has results, no one touches him. It is the same in politics and in other fields.

So it is, Grebenar concludes, in evangelization as well. Whoever has results is protected by God's grace, because he cooperates with it. The interpretation ends with an invitation for believers to humble themselves, "so that God may exalt us as he wills."

sections.subtitle: Od Rame do Imotskog: najave skupova i poziv na podršku centru Kraljica Mira
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj najavljuje promociju knjige u Prozoru i skupove u Dalmaciji
sections.content:
Na kraju emisije Vladimir Grebenar donosi najave za naredne dane. Toga dana, u **subotu 31. listopada**, održava se promocija knjige u **Prozoru (Rama)**, u dvorani hidroelektrane Rama. Slušatelje sa sjevera Hercegovine moli da baner s Facebook stranice Ora et Labora podijele na svojim društvenim mrežama i pozovu nekoga kome bi moglo koristiti da čuje svjedočanstvo i riječ Gospodnju.

Raspored skupova za sljedeći tjedan, uvijek s početkom u 19 sati:

- **ponedjeljak, 2. studenoga**: Biograd na Moru, hotel Ilirija,
- **utorak, 3. studenoga**: Solin, hotel President Solin,
- **srijeda, 4. studenoga**: Imotski, Pučko otvoreno učilište Imotski.

Voditelj savjetuje da posjetitelji dođu ranije kako bi pronašli mjesto. Tjedan nakon toga putuje u Slavoniju, a gradove u kojima će gostovati najavit će naknadno.

Grebenar sve poziva da postanu članovi **domoljubne inicijative Ora et Labora** preko web-stranice diol.hr ili putem objavljenih brojeva mobitela. Prenosi i molbu Hrvata izvan domovine da se pozovu sunarodnjaci iz iseljeništva na **molitvu krunice na glavnom trgu u Zagrebu**, a poziv na molitvu krunice upućuje i svim drugim gradovima.

Emisija završava blagoslovom u ime svete Majke, njezina Sina i svetog Josipa. Uz to voditelj napominje da se kupnjom prve, druge i treće knjige *Isus Lider* pomaže dovršetak **međunarodnog edukacijskog centra Kraljica Mira u Međugorju**. Posljednje su riječi poziv da se Ora et Labora prati svaki dan, „na veću slavu Božju“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je pretežno organizacijski i promiče svjedočenje, molitvu i građanski angažman, bez očite izravne suprotnosti katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu. Poziv na domoljubnu inicijativu i molitvu krunice može biti usklađen s vjerom ako ostaje usmjeren općem dobru i ne poistovjećuje kršćanstvo s političkom ideologijom ili nacionalizmom.
concerns: Izraz da se emisija završava blagoslovom „u ime svete Majke, njezina Sina i svetog Josipa” teološki je neprecizan ako bi sugerirao da su Marija i Josip izvor božanskog blagoslova ili na istoj razini s Kristom; ako se misli na njihovo zagovorništvo, bilo bi korisno to jasnije izraziti.
Domoljubna inicijativa sama po sebi nije problem, no njezin sadržaj i djelovanje trebali bi biti prosuđivani prema evanđeoskim i moralnim načelima, a ne samo prema nacionalnoj pripadnosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Poziv na zajedničku molitvu odgovara biblijskom poticaju da se prinose molitve za sve ljude, a ne samo za vlastitu skupinu; takva molitva treba graditi ljubav i mir, a ne neprijateljstvo prema drugima. Kršćanski angažman u društvu i kulturi može biti vrijedan doprinos zajedničkom dobru, ali ostaje vjeran Evanđelju samo kada poštuje istinu, pravdu i dostojanstvo svake osobe.

Apostolic Journey to Croatia: Meeting with representatives of civil society, the political, academic, cultural, and business world, the diplomatic corps, and religious leaders gathered in the National Croatian Theatre (Zagreb, 4 June 2011)

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is predominantly organizational and promotes witnessing, prayer, and civic engagement, without an obvious direct contradiction to Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture. The call to a patriotic initiative and the prayer of the Rosary can be aligned with faith if it remains directed toward the common good and does not equate Christianity with political ideology or nationalism.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The call to common prayer corresponds to the biblical exhortation that prayers be offered for all people, not only for one's own group; such prayer should build love and peace, rather than hostility toward others. Christian engagement in society and culture can be a valuable contribution to the common good, but remains faithful to the Gospel only when it respects truth, justice, and the dignity of every person.
concerns_en: The expression that the broadcast ends with a blessing „in the name of the holy Mother, her Son, and Saint Joseph” is theologically imprecise if it would suggest that Mary and Joseph are the source of divine blessing or on the same level with Christ; if their intercession is meant, it would be useful to express this more clearly.
A patriotic initiative in itself is not a problem, but its content and action should be judged according to evangelical and moral principles, rather than solely according to national affiliation.

sections.subtitle_en: From Rama to Imotski: announcements of gatherings and invitation to support the Queen of Peace center
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host announces the book promotion in Prozor and gatherings in Dalmatia
sections.content_en:
At the end of the show, Vladimir Grebenar brings announcements for the upcoming days. On that day, **Saturday, October 31**, a book promotion is held in **Prozor (Rama)**, in the hall of the Rama hydroelectric power plant. He asks listeners from northern Herzegovina to share the banner from the Ora et Labora Facebook page on their social networks and invite someone who could benefit from hearing the testimony and the word of the Lord.

Schedule of gatherings for next week, always starting at 7 p.m.:

- **Monday, November 2**: Biograd na Moru, Hotel Ilirija,
- **Tuesday, November 3**: Solin, Hotel President Solin,
- **Wednesday, November 4**: Imotski, Pučko otvoreno učilište Imotski.

The host advises visitors to arrive early to find a seat. The week after that he is traveling to Slavonija, and will announce the host cities later.

Grebenar invites everyone to become members of the **patriotic initiative Ora et Labora** via the website diol.hr or through the published mobile phone numbers. He also conveys a plea from Croats outside the homeland to invite compatriots from the diaspora to **the Rosary prayer in the main square in Zagreb**, and extends the invitation to the Rosary prayer to all other cities as well.

The broadcast ends with a blessing in the name of the Holy Mother, her Son, and Saint Joseph. Additionally, the host notes that the purchase of the first, second, and third *Isus Lider* book helps complete the **Queen of Peace International Educational Center in Međugorje**. The last words are an invitation to follow Ora et Labora every day, "for the greater glory of God."
